subject: Sir2 (yeast)

context.en-US: Sir2 (silent information regulator 2) is the founding member of the sirtuin family, first identified in Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a regulator of mating-type locus silencing and replicative lifespan. The seven mammalian paralogues SIRT1–SIRT7 evolved from this ancestral NAD+-dependent deacetylase, retaining the conserved catalytic core while diversifying in subcellular localization and substrate repertoire. This phylogenetic continuity means insights from yeast Sir2 historically informed mammalian sirtuin biology, although the mammalian enzymes acquired lineage-specific regulatory domains. The relationship is directional: yeast Sir2 is the evolutionary precursor, not a downstream effector, of the SIRT1–7 family.

source_document: Sir2 (yeast).md

subject: Sirtuins

context.en-US: Sirtuins are class III histone deacetylases whose catalytic mechanism absolutely requires NAD+ as a co-substrate, coupling deacetylation to the cellular redox and energy state. Each turnover hydrolyzes one NAD+ molecule into nicotinamide and 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose while removing an acetyl group from a lysine residue on the target protein. This strict NAD+ dependence means sirtuin activity rises when the NAD+/NADH ratio is high, as occurs during caloric restriction, exercise, or fasting, and falls when NAD+ is depleted. A caveat is that this dependency creates competition with other NAD+-consuming enzymes such as CD38 and PARPs for the same limited co-substrate pool.

source_document: Sirtuins.md

subject: Sirtuins

context.en-US: Beyond deacetylation, several sirtuins catalyze mono-ADP-ribosylation, transferring the ADP-ribose moiety of NAD+ onto target proteins without removing an acetyl group. SIRT4 and SIRT6 prominently display this mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity, with SIRT6 using it to recruit heterochromatin proteins such as KAP1/HP1α. The directionality is that NAD+ is the donor and the target lysine (or other residue) is the acceptor, producing a mono-ADP-ribosylated product rather than free OAADPr. Biologically, ADP-ribosylation allows sirtuins to regulate processes—such as DNA repair and LINE-1 repression—distinct from their deacetylase functions.

source_document: Sirtuins.md

subject: Sirtuin deacetylation reaction

context.en-US: During the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation of a lysine, NAD+ is cleaved between its nicotinamide and ADP-ribose moieties, and the acetyl group is transferred to the ADP-ribose to generate 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPr) plus free nicotinamide. OAADPr is a stoichiometric by-product, released in equimolar amounts with the deacetylated substrate on every catalytic cycle. This molecule is not merely waste: it binds and activates the TRPM2 cation channel, linking sirtuin activity to calcium signaling and cellular stress responses. A caveat is that OAADPr accumulation can itself feed back on cellular metabolism, and its levels reflect the integrated deacetylase flux of the cell.

source_document: OAADPr.md

subject: OAADPr

context.en-US: OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose) binds to the cytoplasmic N-terminal domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel, promoting its opening and calcium influx into the cytosol. Because OAADPr is generated directly by sirtuin deacetylase activity, TRPM2 activation acts as a sensor of cellular sirtuin flux and NAD+ utilization. The directionality is unidirectional under basal conditions: sirtuin activity produces OAADPr, which then gates TRPM2, rather than TRPM2 regulating sirtuins. This coupling provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, redox stress, and calcium-dependent processes such as insulin secretion and apoptotic signaling.

source_document: OAADPr.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 is the predominant nuclear sirtuin and is enriched at euchromatic regions, where it deacetylates both histones and many transcriptional regulators to shape gene expression. Its nuclear residence allows it to directly access chromatin and nuclear factors such as p53, FOXO, NF-κB, and PGC-1α. Subcellular localization is dynamic and can shift toward DNA double-strand break foci during genotoxic stress, reflecting its role in DNA repair. A caveat is that a fraction of SIRT1 is also cytosolic, so 'nuclear' describes its dominant but not exclusive compartment.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin and is most abundant in the cytosol, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and a range of metabolic and regulatory proteins. Its localization is cell-cycle regulated, with SIRT2 accumulating and being hyperphosphorylated as cells transit the G2/M boundary. The cytoplasmic residence underpins its roles in microtubule dynamics, mitosis, and cytoplasmic autophagy regulation rather than direct chromatin modification. Note that SIRT2 can also shuttle to the nucleus under certain stress conditions, so localization is not absolute.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 is the principal mitochondrial sirtuin, imported into the matrix where it removes acetyl, succinyl, and other acyl modifications from respiratory-chain and metabolic enzymes. Its activity is governed by the mitochondrial NAD+/NADH ratio, which links the cell's energy state directly to enzyme function, so SIRT3 serves as a metabolic sensor within the organelle. Because of its mitochondrial residence, SIRT3 is positioned to sense and tune local metabolism, driving oxidative phosphorylation, antioxidant defense, and fatty-acid oxidation.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 resides in the mitochondrial matrix and acts mainly as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase on metabolic enzymes such as GDH and MTPα rather than as a conventional deacetylase. Its mitochondrial localization enables direct control of amino-acid and fatty-acid fueling of the TCA cycle, braking anaplerosis and oxidative catabolism. Directionally, SIRT4 is positioned to restrain mitochondrial anabolism, reducing nutrient-driven ATP generation and insulin secretion under replete conditions. This braking role complements SIRT3, which promotes oxidative catabolism, so the SIRT3/SIRT4 balance determines whether mitochondria oxidize or conserve fuel.

source_document: SIRT4.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and is specialized for removing lysine succinyl, malonyl, and glutaryl groups from metabolic enzymes including CPS1, HMGCS2, and enzymes of β-oxidation and the TCA cycle. Its mitochondrial residence makes it a key regulator of catabolic flux during fasting, coordinating nitrogen clearance, ketogenesis, and fatty-acid oxidation. Through desuccinylation it optimizes energy production and redox balance, activating urea-cycle and lipid-catabolism machinery when nutrient supply demands it.

source_document: SIRT5.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 is a nuclear sirtuin enriched at heterochromatic and telomeric regions, where it deacetylates H3K9 and H3K56 and performs mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1. Its heterochromatin association is critical for genome stability, telomere maintenance, and suppression of repetitive elements such as LINE-1. SIRT6 thus integrates chromatin regulation with metabolic control of glycolysis, DNA repair, and inflammation. Loss of SIRT6 produces a pronounced premature-aging phenotype, highlighting its non-redundant role in the nucleus.

source_document: SIRT6.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 is concentrated in the nucleolus, the site of ribosomal DNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis, where it deacetylates histone H3K18 and regulates RNA polymerase I. Its nucleolar residence positions it to control rRNA synthesis and, consequently, protein synthetic capacity and growth. SIRT7 also deacetylates extra-nucleolar targets such as GATA4 and SMAD3, linking it to cardiac and fibrotic pathways. Deficiency of SIRT7 yields extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy, revealing its importance in stress responses of the heart.

source_document: SIRT7.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 functions principally as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase, using NAD+ to attach a single ADP-ribose group to target lysines rather than removing acetyl marks. Its best-characterized ADP-ribosylation target is glutamate dehydrogenase, whose activity it inhibits to dampen amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This enzymatic orientation means SIRT4 generally acts as a metabolic suppressor within mitochondria, opposing anabolic and growth signals. A caveat is that SIRT4's deacetylase activity is weak in vitro, so ADP-ribosylation is its physiologically dominant modality.

source_document: SIRT4.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 possesses both deacetylase and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activities, the latter being particularly important for its chromatin functions. Through ADP-ribosylation of KAP1, SIRT6 recruits HP1α to LINE-1 loci, promoting heterochromatinization and silencing of retrotransposons. The directionality is that SIRT6 is the enzyme and KAP1 (and downstream HP1α) the recipients of the ADP-ribose modification. This activity is independent of its deacetylase function and is selectively enhanced by certain natural activators such as fucoidan.

source_document: SIRT6.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: In yeast, the replicative lifespan extension conferred by caloric restriction is abolished when the SIR2 gene is deleted, establishing Sir2 as a required mediator of the CR response. This dependence reflects the fact that CR raises the NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which relieves nicotinamide feedback inhibition and boosts Sir2 deacetylase activity. The relationship is directional: CR acts upstream and Sir2 is the necessary downstream effector in this genetic pathway. A caveat is that in higher organisms the requirement is distributed across multiple sirtuins and redundant pathways, so SIR2/SIRT1 is necessary but not solely sufficient.

source_document: Sir2 (yeast).md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Reducing glucose from 2% to 0.5% in yeast medium extends replicative lifespan by roughly 30%, an effect mediated through elevated NAD+ availability and Sir2 activation. The mechanism hinges on CR lowering the nicotinamide/NAD+ ratio, thereby disinhibiting Sir2 and reinforcing silencing at repetitive rDNA and subtelomeric regions. This intervention is directional: the dietary manipulation is the cause and the lifespan gain the consequence. The finding seeded the broader hypothesis that sirtuin activation underlies longevity benefits of restricted feeding across species.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Dietary restriction in Drosophila extends lifespan and, as in yeast, this benefit requires the dSir2 (Sir2) gene, indicating evolutionary conservation of the sirtuin-mediated CR pathway. The effect is thought to operate through improved protein homeostasis, stress resistance, and metabolic efficiency rather than simple calorie shortage. Directionally, reduced nutrient signaling upstream engages dSir2 to produce the longevity phenotype. Caveats include that the magnitude and requirement vary with sex, genetic background, and the precise restriction paradigm used.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: In rodents, caloric restriction raises SIRT1 levels in multiple tissues, and this elevation is linked to reduced inflammatory and oxidative responses. Higher SIRT1 expression translates into enhanced deacetylation of targets such as NF-κB, FOXO, and PGC-1α, promoting stress resistance and metabolic health. The directionality is that CR is the upstream stimulus and increased SIRT1 abundance/activity the downstream mediator. This adaptation is considered a key explanation for the anti-aging and disease-protective effects of CR in mammals.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction elevates the brain NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which both supplies more co-substrate for sirtuins and relieves nicotinamide-mediated feedback inhibition of SIRT1. The resulting gain in sirtuin activity supports neuronal stress resistance, mitochondrial function, and suppression of neuroinflammatory signaling. The relationship is directional: CR shifts the ratio upward, which then potentiates sirtuin-dependent protective programs. This mechanism is frequently invoked to explain CR's protective effects against age-related cognitive decline and neurodegenerative pathology.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: In pancreatic islets of calorically restricted mice, SIRT4 expression is reduced, shifting the mitochondrial sirtuin balance toward the protective, oxidative-phosphorylation-promoting actions of SIRT3. Because SIRT4 normally restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial fat oxidation, its downregulation supports improved β-cell metabolic flexibility. The directionality is that CR suppresses SIRT4 transcription, altering the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio. Aging shows the opposite pattern—rising SIRT4 and falling SIRT3—so CR counters the age-related drift in this ratio.

source_document: SIRT4.md

subject: SIR2 overexpression (yeast)

context.en-US: Integration of an extra SIR2 copy in yeast increases replicative lifespan by up to about 30%, implicating Sir2 dosage directly in longevity. The mechanism involves reinforced silencing at rDNA repeats, which reduces spurious recombination and the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles that drive aging. This is a gain-of-function, directional relationship: more Sir2 yields longer lifespan, though the effect saturates and very high doses can be detrimental. The finding established the foundational idea that boosting sirtuin activity can extend lifespan in a simple eukaryote.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Michan_S_Sinclair_D_Sirtuins_in_mammals_insights_i.md

subject: sir-2.1 overexpression (C. elegans)

context.en-US: A chromosomal duplication that increases sir-2.1 dosage in C. elegans extends lifespan by up to approximately 50%, paralleling the yeast finding in a multicellular organism. The longevity effect depends on intact insulin/IGF-1-like signaling, because sir-2.1 acts downstream of the DAF-2 pathway to promote stress resistance. The relationship is directional: elevated sir-2.1 produces the lifespan gain. A key caveat is that the requirement for DAF-16 (FOXO) ties sirtuin longevity to the conserved FOXO transcription-factor network.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Michan_S_Sinclair_D_Sirtuins_in_mammals_insights_i.md

subject: sir-2.1 lifespan extension

context.en-US: The lifespan extension produced by sir-2.1 overexpression in C. elegans is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcription factor DAF-16, the worm FOXO ortholog. DAF-16 is the downstream effector that induces stress-resistance and xenobiotic-detoxification genes once sir-2.1 releases it from repression. Mechanistically, sir-2.1 deacetylates and cooperates with DAF-16 to drive the longevity transcriptional program. Thus the directionality is sir-2.1 → DAF-16 → lifespan, and removing DAF-16 abolishes the benefit.

source_document: DAF-16.md

subject: dSir2 overexpression (Drosophila)

context.en-US: Ubiquitous overexpression of the Drosophila Sir2 ortholog (dSir2) extends female lifespan by about 29%, with a more modest or absent effect in males. The sexually dimorphic response reflects differences in nutrient sensing and reproductive physiology between the sexes, and it mirrors the pattern seen in worm and yeast models. Directionally, increased dSir2 acts upstream to produce the longevity phenotype, consistent with a conserved sirtuin-caloric-restriction axis. As in C. elegans and S. cerevisiae, the effect depends on genetic background, dietary conditions, and the level of expression achieved.

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 at multiple lysine residues, dampening p53's transcriptional activation of pro-apoptotic and senescence genes and promoting cell survival under stress. The modification reduces p53's DNA-binding affinity and coactivator recruitment at target promoters, so SIRT1 effectively restrains the tumor-suppressive output of the protein. This dual role—protective in normal tissue by limiting excessive apoptosis, yet potentially oncogenic by shielding damaged cells—is a defining feature of SIRT1 biology.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 removes acetyl groups from Lys9 and Lys26 of linker histone H1, a modification that influences higher-order chromatin compaction and gene accessibility. Deacetylated H1 is generally associated with a more condensed, transcriptionally repressed chromatin state at SIRT1-target loci. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts enzymatically on H1 to remodel chromatin and silence specific programs. Because H1 links nucleosomes, this action helps SIRT1 enforce long-range repression independently of core histone modifications.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys14 of histone H3 (H3K14ac), a mark associated with active transcription, thereby contributing to gene silencing at targeted promoters. Loss of H3K14ac reduces promoter accessibility and cooperates with other repressive modifications to restrain transcription, making this a mechanism of chromatin-level control. Directionally, SIRT1 acts enzymatically to remove the acetyl mark and shift chromatin toward repression. This histone-targeting activity complements SIRT1 deacetylation of non-histone substrates and helps explain how a single sirtuin coordinates broad transcriptional programs across the genome.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 removes the acetyl group from Lys16 of histone H4, a site whose acetylation is linked to telomeric and rDNA silencing and genome stability. Deacetylation at H4K16 promotes a more compact chromatin fiber and is shared with SIRT2 at this residue in certain contexts. The relationship is directional and repressive: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation consolidates heterochromatin-like states. Defective H4K16 deacetylation is associated with the genomic instability seen when SIRT1 function is compromised.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of p53

context.en-US: By deacetylating p53, SIRT1 lowers p53's transcriptional activation of BH3-only proteins and other apoptotic effectors, suppressing programmed cell death after oxidative or genotoxic stress. This creates a survival bias that helps cells tolerate damage but can also protect incipient cancer cells from elimination. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity on p53 is upstream of reduced apoptosis. A caveat is that chronic suppression of p53-dependent apoptosis is a double-edged sword: protective in normal tissue but potentially tumor-promoting.

source_document: README.md

subject: HIC1

context.en-US: HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) is a tumor suppressor that binds the SIRT1 promoter via its POZ domain and directly represses SIRT1 transcription. Because p53 transactivates HIC1, a negative feedback loop exists: p53 induces HIC1, which then restrains SIRT1, preventing excessive p53 deacetylation and preserving p53 tumor-suppressive capacity. The directionality is HIC1 → SIRT1 repression, upstream of SIRT1's inhibition of p53. Disruption of this loop in cancer can unleash SIRT1 to silence p53.

source_document: HIC1.md

subject: p53

context.en-US: p53 directly activates transcription of HIC1, a tumor suppressor that in turn represses the SIRT1 promoter, forming a negative feedback loop that restrains SIRT1 abundance. This loop ensures that p53 activity is not indefinitely suppressed by SIRT1-mediated deacetylation, because sustained p53 signaling drives HIC1 to limit SIRT1 expression. Directionally, p53 is the transcription factor and HIC1 the induced target gene, with SIRT1 sitting downstream of both. The biological significance is genome protection: by inducing HIC1, p53 prevents SIRT1 from over-deacetylating and silencing p53 itself, preserving the capacity for apoptosis and senescence in response to damage.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates Ku70 (Cohen 2004), the DNA-repair factor and Ku-complex subunit that also binds and inhibits the pro-apoptotic protein Bax. Deacetylation increases Ku70's affinity for Bax, sequestering Bax away from mitochondria and preventing outer-membrane permeabilization, coupling DNA-damage signaling to cell-survival decisions. This links SIRT1's genome-maintenance functions to a direct anti-apoptotic program; in some cancers the same axis helps tumor cells evade death, showing how a survival pathway can be co-opted in oncogenesis.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Deacetylated Ku70

context.en-US: Once deacetylated by SIRT1, Ku70 binds the BH3 domain of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and retains it in the cytosol, preventing Bax translocation to and permeabilization of mitochondria. This sequestration blocks the intrinsic apoptosis cascade downstream of many stress signals, including DNA damage and oxidative stress. Directionally, deacetylated Ku70 is the binding partner that neutralizes Bax, converting a DNA-repair factor into an anti-apoptotic scaffold. The net effect is cytoprotection, though as with p53 suppression this can also shield damaged cells in oncogenic contexts, where the Ku70–Bax interaction becomes a target for restoring apoptosis in cancer therapy.

source_document: Ku70.md

subject: E2F1

context.en-US: The E2F1 transcription factor binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and activates its transcription, particularly under proliferative or DNA-damage signals. This positions SIRT1 as a downstream effector of E2F1-driven programs that balance cell-cycle progression with survival. Directionally, E2F1 acts upstream of SIRT1 gene activation, linking growth signals to increased sirtuin abundance. Notably, the relationship is reciprocal, because SIRT1 then feeds back to deacetylate and inhibit E2F1's apoptotic function, creating a regulatory loop in which E2F1 both induces its own regulator and is constrained by it—a circuit relevant to tumor suppression and the DNA-damage response.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 interacts with and deacetylates E2F1, converting it from a potent inducer of apoptosis into a less active transcriptional partner and thereby blocking E2F1-dependent cell death. This creates a feedback loop in which E2F1 induces SIRT1, and SIRT1 then restrains E2F1's apoptotic output. The directionality is SIRT1 acting upstream to suppress E2F1's deadly transcriptional program. The net consequence is enhanced cell survival under stress, with implications for both tissue homeostasis and tumorigenesis.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates the forkhead factor FOXO1, redirecting its transcriptional program toward metabolic homeostasis and stress resistance while tempering apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO1 cooperates with C/EBPα to induce adiponectin and with PGC-1α to support oxidative metabolism, gluconeogenesis, and antioxidant gene expression. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies FOXO1 to reshape its target-gene output. This regulation is central to SIRT1's control of glucose handling and insulin sensitivity, and the two proteins form a positive feedback loop in which FOXO1 also activates the SIRT1 promoter, amplifying stress-resistance and metabolic-adaptation programs across tissues.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a in multiple cell types, including neurons and fibroblasts, shifting its target-gene program toward stress resistance and away from apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO3a induces antioxidant enzymes such as SOD2 and catalase, promotes autophagy and mitophagy through BNIP3, and reduces death-gene expression, biasing cells toward repair and survival. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies FOXO3a, and the altered transcription follows downstream. This stress-resistant switch is central to SIRT1-mediated protection in aging and neurodegeneration, and it links sirtuin activity to redox homeostasis and cellular quality control.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO4, which reverts FOXO4-mediated suppression and enhances cellular defenses against oxidative stress. Deacetylation of FOXO4 boosts expression of DNA-repair and antioxidant genes such as GADD45 while suppressing caspase activation, steering cells toward genome maintenance rather than death. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 enzymatically licenses FOXO4 to drive protective transcription. This contributes to SIRT1's broad role in genomic maintenance and resilience to damage, and parallels SIRT1's regulation of other FOXO family members, with the balance among FOXO1, FOXO3a, and FOXO4 shaping tissue-specific stress responses and survival decisions.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates the RelA/p65 subunit of NF-κB, particularly at Lys310, reducing its ability to recruit the transcriptional machinery and activate pro-inflammatory genes. This post-translational modification dampens NF-κB target genes such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, and also licenses p65 for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation, further lowering inflammatory output. Directionally, SIRT1 acts enzymatically on RelA to inhibit inflammatory transcription. Because NF-κB drives chronic inflammation implicated in aging and disease, SIRT1's action is a key anti-inflammatory node, and loss of SIRT1 or its decline with age allows NF-κB activity to rise and perpetuate low-grade systemic inflammation.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of RelA/p65

context.en-US: Deacetylation of RelA/p65 by SIRT1 lowers NF-κB transactivation, thereby reducing expression of cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules that propagate inflammation. This directly opposes the pro-inflammatory program and underlies many of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative contexts. The directionality is SIRT1 deacetylation → suppressed NF-κB signaling. A caveat is that excessive NF-κB suppression could impair host defense, so the effect is beneficial within physiological ranges.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: Cigarette smoke

context.en-US: Exposure to cigarette-smoke extract disrupts the SIRT1–RelA/p65 complex, diminishing deacetylation of RelA and leaving NF-κB in a more active, pro-inflammatory state. The consequence is heightened expression of inflammatory mediators in airway and other cells exposed to smoke. The directionality is that the environmental insult (smoke) reduces a protective protein–protein interaction, increasing inflammation. This provides a mechanistic link between smoking, impaired sirtuin function, and chronic inflammatory lung disease.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 expression is significantly elevated in breast carcinoma compared with normal breast tissue, and high SIRT7 correlates with poorer prognosis in several tumor types. Its overexpression supports tumor growth and ribosomal biogenesis, and it can deacetylate oncogenic transcription factors such as GATA4. The directionality is that increased SIRT7 abundance is associated with and likely promotes malignant phenotypes. A caveat is that sirtuin roles in cancer are context-dependent, and SIRT7 can be either tumor-promoting or, in some tissues, tumor-suppressive.

source_document: SIRT7.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 activates RNA polymerase I-mediated transcription of ribosomal DNA, driving ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity in proliferating cells. It does so in part through deacetylation of histone H3K18 at rDNA loci and by stabilizing the Pol I transcriptional apparatus, ensuring sufficient ribosome output for growth. Directionally, SIRT7 acts upstream to enhance rRNA production and ribosome biogenesis. By sustaining this biosynthetic capacity, SIRT7 supports cell growth and proliferation, which underlies its roles in development and in cancer, where ribosome biogenesis is frequently upregulated.

source_document: SIRT7.md

subject: SIRT1
object: RNA Polymerase I transcription (via TAFI68 deacetylation)

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates TAFI68, a subunit of the RNA polymerase I transcription factor complex, decreasing its DNA-binding activity and thereby repressing rRNA transcription. This contrasts with SIRT7, which activates Pol I, illustrating divergent sirtuin control of ribosome biogenesis within the same family. Directionally, SIRT1 acts on TAFI68 to repress Pol I output. By limiting ribosome production, SIRT1 can restrain growth and oppose the biosynthetic programs favored in cancer and pathological hypertrophy, positioning the SIRT1/SIRT7 balance as a rheostat that determines whether cells commit to growth-oriented or maintenance-oriented metabolism.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 resides in a genomic region frequently deleted in human gliomas, and re-expression of SIRT2 markedly reduces colony formation by glioma cells, indicating tumor-suppressor function. Its activity deacetylates substrates such as α-tubulin and HNF4α that govern mitotic fidelity and metabolism, helping to preserve genomic stability during division. Directionally, SIRT2 loss permits gliomagenesis while SIRT2 restoration suppresses it. A caveat is that SIRT2 can act as either a tumor suppressor or a promoter depending on tissue and context—stabilizing oncogenes like c-Myc in some settings—so its role in cancer is highly context-dependent and cell-type-specific.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 deacetylates Lys16 on histone H4 (H4K16ac), a modification linked to chromatin condensation during the G2/M transition of mitosis. Removing H4K16ac promotes a more compact mitotic chromatin state compatible with chromosome segregation and mitotic fidelity. Enzymatically, SIRT2 directly deacetylates H4K16 to remodel chromatin at division, complementing its actions on α-tubulin and mitotic regulators. This chromatin function, together with SIRT2's peak expression at G2/M, couples deacetylation to cell-cycle control, and its loss is associated with mitotic defects, genomic instability, and, in some cancers, tumor progression.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT2 expression

context.en-US: SIRT2 protein levels rise dramatically as cells enter mitosis, and the enzyme is hyperphosphorylated at the G2/M boundary, timing its activity to chromosome condensation and division. This cell-cycle coupling links SIRT2 to proper mitotic progression and genomic stability, with the enzyme regulating both tubulin dynamics and chromatin state during division. Directionally, the G2/M transition drives SIRT2 upregulation and activation, and at mitotic exit the phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2 to trigger its degradation. Loss or dysregulation of this mitotic peak is associated with aneuploidy, mitotic defects, and, in some cancers, genomic instability.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT6 knockout mice

context.en-US: Mice lacking SIRT6 develop a striking premature-aging syndrome with reduced size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphopenia, colitis, and spinal curvature, dying early in life. The phenotype reflects defective base-excision repair, genomic instability, and metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation, demonstrating that SIRT6 is essential for maintaining genome integrity and metabolic homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency produces multisystem premature aging. This makes SIRT6 one of the clearest single-gene links between sirtuins and mammalian longevity, and it positions SIRT6 among the strongest candidates for translating sirtuin biology into interventions that delay age-related decline.

source_document: SIRT6.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 is required for efficient base-excision repair (BER), the pathway that removes oxidized and alkylated bases, and SIRT6-deficient cells accumulate DNA damage from defective BER. SIRT6 supports BER in part by mono-ADP-ribosylating and recruiting repair factors such as PARP1 and by maintaining heterochromatin at damaged sites. Directionally, SIRT6 activity sits upstream of proper BER execution. This function explains the genomic instability and premature aging of SIRT6 knockout mice, and links SIRT6 to tumor suppression, since loss of SIRT6-dependent repair predisposes cells to mutation accumulation and oncogenic transformation.

source_document: SIRT6.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys50 of the HIV-1 transactivator Tat, a modification that increases Tat's affinity for the viral LTR and its ability to recruit the transcription machinery. This enzymatic action therefore activates, rather than suppresses, the viral protein, promoting robust expression of viral genes from the proviral genome. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies Tat and thereby enhances viral transcription, revealing an unexpected pro-viral role for the otherwise cytoprotective SIRT1. Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, the interaction represents a host factor that HIV exploits, making SIRT1–Tat a candidate target for antiviral strategies.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of Tat

context.en-US: Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation at Lys50 boosts HIV-1 transcription from the proviral LTR. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Tat to amplify viral gene expression and reactivate latent proviruses. This positions host SIRT1 as a cofactor that HIV exploits, a caveat to the generally beneficial reputation of SIRT1 activation. Targeting this interaction is of interest for antiviral strategies, particularly for the shock-and-kill approach to HIV latency, where compounds that modulate the SIRT1–Tat axis could either silence or purge the latent reservoir depending on the therapeutic goal.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: In white adipose tissue, SIRT1 promotes lipolysis and fat mobilization by repressing adipogenic transcription factors such as PPAR-γ and aP2 and by co-ordinating catabolic gene programs. This shifts storage tissue from lipid accumulation toward fatty-acid release for oxidation in muscle and liver, supporting metabolic flexibility. Directionally, SIRT1 acts to repress adipogenesis and enhance fat mobilization. These actions contribute to the lean phenotype and metabolic health seen under caloric restriction, and reduced SIRT1 in visceral adipose stem cells from obese individuals is associated with enhanced adipogenic capacity and visceral fat expansion.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 represses PPAR-γ, the master regulator of adipogenesis, by deacetylating it and interfering with its co-activator interactions, thereby inhibiting differentiation of preadipocytes into fat cells. Pharmacological SIRT1 activation or overexpression recapitulates this repression and blocks adipogenesis, while SIRT1 knockdown promotes adipogenic differentiation. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PPAR-γ suppression, limiting fat-cell formation. By restraining adipogenesis, SIRT1 prevents excessive white-fat accumulation and contributes to the metabolic benefits of caloric restriction, although its role in mature adipocytes and lipid mobilization is more complex.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: PGC-1α

context.en-US: PGC-1α is the master coactivator controlling mitochondrial biogenesis, stimulating transcription of nuclear-encoded respiratory-chain subunits and coordinating with mitochondrial DNA replication. Its activation by SIRT1, through deacetylation, and by AMPK, through phosphorylation, increases mitochondrial number and oxidative capacity in response to energy demand. Directionally, PGC-1α sits upstream of new mitochondrion formation, partnering with NRF1, NRF2, ERRα, and TFAM to execute the program.
context.zh-TW: PGC-1α 是調節粒線體生成與細胞能量代謝的重要轉錄共活化因子，包括呼吸鏈複合體的形成以及粒線體分裂與融合等過程。研究發現 urolithin A 增強 PGC-1α 的表現與活化，改善粒線體功能並增加粒線體數量，這對確保充足的肌肉能量供應並支持耐力表現至關重要。因此，PGC-1α 活化是 urolithin A 對粒線體健康效應的核心機制。

source_document: Mitochondrial Biogenesis.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 transcriptionally represses UCP2, a mitochondrial inner-membrane uncoupler that dissipates the proton gradient and reduces ATP yield. In SIRT1 knockout mice, UCP2 is upregulated, lowering ATP production in pancreatic β-cells and impairing glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Directionally, SIRT1 suppresses UCP2 expression to preserve the mitochondrial membrane potential needed for efficient ATP generation. By keeping UCP2 low, SIRT1 maintains bioenergetic efficiency in β-cells and other tissues, linking sirtuin activity to glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and protection against the β-cell dysfunction that characterizes type 2 diabetes.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 repression of UCP2

context.en-US: Repression of UCP2 by SIRT1 preserves mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis in pancreatic β-cells, which raises the ATP/ADP ratio and closes KATP channels to trigger insulin release. Mice overexpressing SIRT1 in β-cells show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, while SIRT1 loss elevates UCP2 and impairs the response. Directionally, SIRT1-mediated UCP2 downregulation leads to stronger insulin secretion. This links SIRT1 to improved glucose homeostasis and protection against diabetes, and it is consistent with the observation that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, preserves β-cell function and insulin sensitivity in aging organisms.

source_document: GLUT2.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (AceCS2) in the mitochondrial matrix, enabling it to convert acetate into acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle and lipogenesis. Deacetylation relieves autoinhibition, increasing AceCS2's catalytic efficiency and allowing mitochondria to use acetate as an alternative carbon source. Directionally, SIRT3 activates AceCS2 to drive mitochondrial acetyl-CoA production. This supports metabolic flexibility during fasting and alcohol metabolism, when acetate is abundant, and parallels SIRT1's activation of the cytoplasmic isoform AceCS1, demonstrating that sirtuins broadly license acetate salvage across both mitochondrial and cytosolic compartments.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (AceCS1) in the cytoplasm, analogous to SIRT3's activation of the mitochondrial AceCS2, permitting acetate utilization outside the mitochondrion. Activated AceCS1 supplies cytosolic acetyl-CoA for chromatin modification, fatty-acid synthesis, and other biosynthetic reactions. Directionally, SIRT1 activates AceCS1 to feed cytosolic acetyl-CoA metabolism. Together with SIRT3, this shows sirtuins broadly license acetate salvage across compartments, coupling nutrient availability and redox state to acetyl-CoA pools that influence both bioenergetics and the epigenetic regulation of gene expression.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 lowers mitochondrial ROS by deacetylating and activating antioxidant enzymes such as MnSOD and components of the electron-transport chain, while also reducing mitochondrial membrane potential in a manner that limits superoxide leak. Higher SIRT3 activity therefore shifts the mitochondrial redox balance toward less oxidative damage. The directionality is SIRT3 activity upstream of reduced ROS. This antioxidant function is a major basis for SIRT3's protective roles in heart, liver, and aging.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: Cold exposure induces SIRT3 in brown adipose tissue, where it promotes expression of mitochondrial genes and supports thermogenic programs. The induction enhances oxidative metabolism and uncoupled respiration needed for heat production, with SIRT3 acting upstream of UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Directionally, a cold stimulus triggers SIRT3 upregulation, which in turn drives thermogenic mitochondrial biogenesis. This ties SIRT3 to adaptive thermogenesis and the metabolic benefits of cold exposure, and conversely SIRT3 is reduced in brown adipose tissue of obese mice, linking obesity to impaired thermogenic capacity and blunted cold-induced mitochondrial function.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 mono-ADP-ribosylates glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), inhibiting its oxidative deamination of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and thereby slowing anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. This restrains amino-acid-derived ATP production and insulin secretion in pancreatic β-cells, limiting nutrient-driven hormonal output. Directionally, SIRT4 enzymatically inhibits GDH, acting as a mitochondrial brake on amino-acid catabolism. This opposes anabolic fueling of secretion, and because SIRT4 also inhibits MTPα, glutamine metabolism, and PPARα signaling, it broadly curbs mitochondrial oxidative capacity while promoting lipid conservation under nutrient-replete conditions.

source_document: SIRT4.md

subject: SIRT4 inhibition of GDH

context.en-US: By inhibiting GDH, SIRT4 blunts the ability of amino acids such as leucine to stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β-cells, because less α-ketoglutarate is generated to elevate ATP and trigger secretion. The relationship is directional: SIRT4-mediated GDH inhibition reduces amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion, restraining the nutrient-dependent arm of insulin release. This positions SIRT4 as a physiological negative regulator of nutrient-stimulated insulin secretion, complementary to SIRT1's positive effects on glucose-stimulated secretion.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Michan_S_Sinclair_D_Sirtuins_in_mammals_insights_i.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 protects neurons from β-amyloid-induced toxicity, in part by inhibiting NF-κB signaling in microglia and reducing neuroinflammation, and by supporting neuronal stress-resistance pathways. This limits the inflammatory and oxidative damage that accompany amyloid pathology and preserves synaptic function. Directionally, SIRT1 activity sits upstream of reduced neuronal injury. The effect dovetails with observations that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, protects against Alzheimer's-like neuropathology in mouse models, and that SIRT1 promotes non-amyloidogenic processing of APP through the α-secretase ADAM10, reducing production of the toxic β-amyloid peptide itself.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 confers neuroprotection partly through deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α, which drives mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defenses in neurons. Enhanced PGC-1α activity counters the energetic and oxidative deficits underlying neurodegeneration, and PGC-1α knockout mice are markedly more sensitive to toxins such as MPTP and kainic acid. Directionally, SIRT1 activates PGC-1α to build neuronal resilience. This axis is a leading explanation for how SIRT1 activation benefits Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and other neurodegenerative models, and it connects sirtuin biology to mitochondrial health as a central determinant of neuronal survival in aging.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Resveratrol

context.en-US: Resveratrol, a red-wine polyphenol, was the first widely studied small-molecule activator of mammalian SIRT1 and is a prototypical sirtuin-activating compound (STAC) (Howitz et al., 2003, Nature 425:191-196, PMID 12805428; Baur et al., 2006, Nature 444:337-342, PMID 17086191). It binds the SIRT1 N-terminal domain near Glu230, lowering the enzyme's Km for peptide and NAD+ substrates (K-type allosteric activation), and additionally engages an indirect cAMP/PDE4/Epac1/AMPK/NAD+ cascade. Activation extends lifespan in yeast, worms, flies, and high-calorie-diet mice, though poor oral bioavailability limits in vivo relevance.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Resveratrol

context.en-US: Resveratrol extends lifespan in yeast through a Sir2-dependent mechanism, mirroring the effect of caloric restriction and establishing it as a prototypical sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). The lifespan gain requires the SIR2 gene, confirming that the compound works through the sirtuin axis rather than an independent pathway. Directionally, resveratrol activates Sir2 to promote longevity. These findings, reported by Howitz and Sinclair in 2003 (PMID 12939617), launched the modern field of sirtuin-targeted longevity therapeutics and led directly to the discovery of additional STACs and the clinical development of sirtuin activators for age-related disease.

source_document: _document_ - berrougui2009_resveratrol_as_atheroprotective_compound.md

subject: Resveratrol

context.en-US: Resveratrols lifespan-extending effect in yeast is absolutely dependent on the presence of the SIR2 gene, so SIR2 deletion abolishes the benefit. This genetic requirement demonstrated that resveratrol acts through sirtuin activation rather than through off-target longevity pathways, and it provided the first causal evidence linking a natural compound to sirtuin-dependent lifespan extension. Directionally, resveratrol acts upstream while SIR2 is the necessary downstream effector. This landmark 2003 finding launched the search for sirtuin-activating compounds and established the framework for testing whether pharmacological sirtuin activation can reproduce the benefits of caloric restriction.

source_document: Sir2 (yeast).md

subject: Resveratrol (high-calorie diet mice)

context.en-US: In mice on a high-calorie diet, resveratrol increases mitochondrial number and function, an effect accompanied by elevated SIRT1 and PGC-1α activity. This shift counters diet-induced metabolic dysfunction by improving oxidative capacity, increasing endurance, and protecting against the metabolic consequences of overnutrition. Directionally, resveratrol activates SIRT1/PGC-1α to drive mitochondrial biogenesis. The finding, from Baur and Sinclair's 2006 study in Cell, helped popularize resveratrol as a caloric-restriction mimetic against diet-induced obesity and demonstrated that a small molecule could reproduce key metabolic benefits of dietary restriction in mammals.

source_document: Mitochondrial Biogenesis.md

subject: Resveratrol

context.en-US: Resveratrol treatment lowers blood glucose and circulating insulin in animals on a high-calorie diet, improving glycemic control and insulin sensitivity. These metabolic benefits are linked to SIRT1/AMPK activation and improved insulin signaling in liver and muscle, together with reduced hepatic steatosis. Directionally, resveratrol activates SIRT1/AMPK to lower glycemia. Caveats include that human trials have been inconsistent, likely owing to the compound's poor oral bioavailability, short half-life, and extensive first-pass metabolism, which limit the translation of preclinical efficacy to physiological exposures achievable through dietary or supplement intake in people.

subject: SIRT3 gene variant (intron 5 enhancer)

context.en-US: A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity, specifically survival beyond 90 years in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance and antioxidant capacity. Directionally, the genetic variation is associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation it supports—but does not prove—that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity, and it is consistent with separate findings linking SIRT3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms to longevity in other cohorts, including the TRELONG study, reinforcing SIRT3 as a candidate human longevity gene.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: SIRT1 allele variants

context.en-US: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel at rest and during activity. Directionally, genetic SIRT1 variation is linked to an energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most genetic-association findings, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent, and replication in other populations is needed.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 binds the androgen receptor and deacetylates it at Lys630 within its lysine-rich motif, repressing AR transcriptional activity and its oncogenic signaling in prostate tissue. This enzymatic modification dampens AR-driven proliferative and survival programs, opposing androgen-dependent growth. Directionally, SIRT1 acts upstream to inhibit AR function. This axis is relevant to prostate cancer, where SIRT1 can oppose androgen-dependent tumor growth, and it suggests that sirtuin activators might complement androgen-deprivation therapies. The interaction also illustrates SIRT1's broader capacity to restrain nuclear-receptor signaling in steroid-responsive tissues.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 interacts with HOXA10, a conserved homeobox transcription factor critical for embryonic cell-type determination and adult tissue homeostasis, including reproductive and hematopoietic development. The interaction suggests SIRT2 influences HOXA10-dependent transcriptional programs, though the precise deacetylation outcome is less well characterized than for other SIRT2 substrates. Directionally, SIRT2 engages HOXA10 as a partner and potential substrate. This connection links SIRT2 to developmental regulation and possibly to differentiation defects in disease, and is consistent with SIRT2's broader roles in controlling transcription-factor activity and cell-fate decisions across tissues.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 physically interacts with the bHLH transcriptional repressors Hes1 and Hey2 both in vitro and in vivo, modulating their ability to repress target promoters. Deacetylation by SIRT1 can alter the DNA-binding or co-repressor recruitment of these factors, tuning the strength of Notch-and-Hes-coupled gene silencing. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modulates Hes1/Hey2 repression. This intersects with Notch and VEGF signaling and with SIRT1's neuroprotective regulation of BDNF, since Hes1 is a repressor of the BDNF promoter and SIRT1 relieves that repression through Hes1 deacetylation, linking this interaction to neuronal survival and cognitive function.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1-null mice are markedly smaller, grow slowly, and show defects in eye morphogenesis and cardiac septation, revealing SIRT1's role in normal development. These phenotypes indicate that SIRT1 is not merely a stress-response protein but is required for organogenesis and systemic growth. Directionally, SIRT1 deficiency causes structural developmental abnormalities. The perinatal lethality of many SIRT1 knockout strains limited study of the complete phenotype, prompting the development of tissue-specific conditional models that have since clarified SIRT1's contributions to metabolism, circadian rhythm, fertility, and stress resistance in the adult organism.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: Surviving SIRT1 knockout mice of both sexes are sterile: males have low sperm counts and females fail to ovulate, implicating SIRT1 in gametogenesis and reproductive endocrine control. The defect reflects failed differentiation and stress responses in gonadal tissues, where SIRT1 normally supports germ-cell survival and maturation. Directionally, SIRT1 loss leads to reproductive failure. This shows SIRT1 is essential for germ-cell development and fertility, and it is consistent with SIRT1's broader role in integrating nutrient status with reproductive function—a link relevant to the well-known dependence of fertility on metabolic state in mammals.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Nmnat (NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme)

context.en-US: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons, preserving axon integrity when the soma is damaged. Directionally, Nmnat increases NAD+, which activates SIRT1 to provide axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience, informed subsequent studies of SARM1-mediated NAD+ depletion in axonal degeneration, and helped motivate the use of NAD+ precursors such as NMN and NR to protect neurons.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Michan_S_Sinclair_D_Sirtuins_in_mammals_insights_i.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates Smad7 at Lys60 and Lys70, which enhances Smad7's recognition by the E3 ligase Smurf1 and targets it for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation. This accelerates turnover of the TGF-β inhibitory Smad, modulating the intensity and duration of TGF-β pathway signaling. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically marks Smad7 for destruction. The consequence is context-dependent regulation of TGF-β signaling rather than simple inhibition: by limiting the negative-feedback inhibitor Smad7, SIRT1 can fine-tune TGF-β responses in kidney, where this mechanism protects glomerular cells from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis during injury.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of Smad7

context.en-US: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output in the kidney. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies, where excessive TGF-β drives mesangial injury and fibrosis. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate during injury, and it complements SIRT1's broader antifibrotic actions that suppress TGF-β1-induced apoptosis, fibrosis, and CTGF expression in renal tissue.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys115 and Lys121 of the histone variant H2A.Z, a mark that licenses H2A.Z for ubiquitination and proteasome-dependent degradation. Removing these acetyl groups thus destabilizes H2A.Z at chromatin and reduces its occupancy at target promoters. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies H2A.Z upstream of its clearance from chromatin. Because H2A.Z promotes pathological gene programs, including those driving maladaptive cardiac hypertrophy, its removal by SIRT1 is protective in the heart, and this mechanism illustrates how a sirtuin can shape transcription by controlling the stability of a histone variant rather than only its acetylation state.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of H2A.Z

context.en-US: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation and degradation of H2A.Z helps protect the heart from failure by removing a histone variant that drives maladaptive cardiac hypertrophic gene programs. Deacetylated H2A.Z is targeted for proteasomal degradation, reducing its presence at promoters that would otherwise sustain pathological remodeling. Directionally, SIRT1 promotes H2A.Z loss, which attenuates hypertrophy. This is a mechanistically plausible explanation for why SIRT1 activation is cardioprotective, though the in vivo evidence carries moderate confidence.

source_document: Cardiac Hypertrophy.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 negatively regulates the histone acetyltransferase p300 by deacetylating it at Lys1020 and Lys1024, reducing p300's enzymatic and coactivator activity. This counterbalances p300-driven acetylation of chromatin and transcription factors, creating a rheostat between opposing acetylation and deacetylation reactions. Directionally, SIRT1 inhibits a major acetyltransferase to enforce gene repression. This crosstalk helps SIRT1 repress inflammatory and growth genes, and it shows that sirtuins tune the acetylation machinery itself, not only individual substrates—an important layer of regulation given that p300 acetylates histones and factors such as p53, NF-κB, and MyoD.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 is expressed in oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, the myelin-forming glia of the CNS and PNS respectively, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and regulates microtubule stability. Its presence in myelinating cells ties SIRT2 to axonal support, myelin integrity, and the cytoskeletal dynamics required for glial process extension. Directionally, SIRT2 acts within glia to control cytoskeletal organization. Dysregulation of SIRT2 is implicated in demyelinating and neurodegenerative conditions, and because α-tubulin acetylation is protective in axons, the balance of SIRT2 activity in myelinating glia is thought to influence both myelination and axonal health.

source_document: SIRT2.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 inhibits myogenesis by deacetylating histones H3K9 and H3K14 at the promoters of myogenin and myosin heavy chain, repressing muscle-gene expression. This keeps myoblasts in a less differentiated state under certain conditions, opposing the myogenic program driven by MyoD and MEF2. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed muscle differentiation. However, SIRT1 can also support muscle maintenance under stress, so context matters: SIRT1 also deacetylates PCAF and MyoD themselves to restrain differentiation, yet in aging or metabolic stress it protects muscle from damage, illustrating that SIRT1's net effect on muscle depends on the balance of these opposing actions.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 activators promote osteoblast differentiation while suppressing adipocyte formation from mesenchymal progenitors, biasing lineage commitment toward bone. This effect is linked to SIRT1's repression of PPAR-γ and support of RUNX2/osteogenic programs. The directionality is SIRT1 favoring osteogenesis over adipogenesis. The association carries moderate confidence (0.75) but has therapeutic implications for osteoporosis. Importantly, it complements SIRT1's opposing action on myogenesis, underscoring context dependence.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: p33ING1b

context.en-US: In hepatocarcinoma, p33ING1b binds SIRT1 and blocks its ability to deacetylate p53, thereby preserving p53's transcriptional activity, including repression of α-fetoprotein (AFP). This relieves SIRT1-mediated inhibition of p53 tumor suppression, restoring the p53-dependent checkpoint in liver cancer cells. Directionally, p33ING1b antagonizes SIRT1 at the p53 node. The interaction reveals a tissue-specific brake on SIRT1's pro-survival, potentially oncogenic action, and is consistent with p33ING1b's function as a tumor suppressor that cooperates with p53, highlighting how accessory proteins can redirect sirtuin activity toward anti-tumor outcomes.

source_document: p33ING1b.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO1 and enhances its interaction with C/EBPα, a combination that drives transcription of the adiponectin gene and raises circulating adiponectin. Adiponectin in turn improves insulin sensitivity and has anti-inflammatory effects in liver and muscle. Directionally, SIRT1 acts through FOXO1 and C/EBPα to promote adiponectin expression. This links SIRT1 to beneficial adipokine secretion and metabolic health, and forms part of a positive circuit in which SIRT1-mediated adiponectin induction reinforces systemic insulin sensitivity, consistent with the insulin-sensitizing phenotype associated with SIRT1 activation and caloric restriction.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: Adiponectin

context.en-US: Administration of adiponectin to obese, high-fat-fed mice improves insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose, reflecting its role as an insulin-sensitizing adipokine. It acts through the AdipoR1/2 receptors to activate AMPK and PPAR-α pathways that enhance fatty-acid oxidation and glucose uptake. Directionally, adiponectin sits upstream of improved insulin action in peripheral tissues. Because SIRT1 raises adiponectin via the FOXO1–C/EBPα axis, this forms part of SIRT1's anti-diabetic circuitry, and declining adiponectin with obesity contributes to the insulin resistance that sirtuin-activating interventions aim to reverse.

source_document: Adiponectin.md

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: In mouse models engineered to develop Alzheimer's-like pathology, caloric restriction prevents accumulation of β-amyloid neuropathology, an effect consistent with SIRT1-driven reductions in neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. CR also preserves cognitive function and synaptic integrity in these models. Directionally, caloric restriction sits upstream of reduced amyloid burden. This supports the hypothesis that CR protects the brain through sirtuin-mediated resilience, and is consistent with SIRT1's promotion of the non-amyloidogenic α-secretase ADAM10. Human translation remains uncertain, but the findings motivate lifestyle interventions and NAD+-boosting strategies in neurodegeneration.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: PGC-1α knockout mice
object: MPTP and kainic acid neuronal damage

context.en-US: Mice lacking PGC-1α are markedly more sensitive to neuronal loss induced by MPTP, a dopaminergic toxin, and kainic acid, an excitotoxin, revealing PGC-1αs role in neuronal stress resistance. Because SIRT1 activates PGC-1α by deacetylation, this sensitivity indirectly implicates the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis in neuroprotection. Directionally, PGC-1α deficiency heightens vulnerability to these insults, while its activation confers resistance. Since PGC-1α drives mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant gene expression, protecting neurons through this axis is a proposed strategy against Parkinsons disease and other neurodegenerative disorders.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: Sirtuins

context.en-US: The sirtuin family comprises seven mammalian members (SIRT1–SIRT7) plus the ancestral yeast Sir2, all sharing an NAD+-dependent catalytic core that performs deacetylation and ADP-ribosylation. They differ in subcellular localization—nuclear (SIRT1, SIRT6, SIRT7), cytoplasmic (SIRT2), and mitochondrial (SIRT3, SIRT4, SIRT5)—which dictates their substrate portfolios. The directionality is that NAD+ is the obligate co-substrate for every family member. This unifying dependence ties sirtuin activity to the cellular energy and redox state.

source_document: Sirtuins.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates PGC-1alpha (Rodgers 2005 PMID 15931387), switching it from a repressed to an active transcriptional coactivator that drives mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes. Deacetylated PGC-1alpha enters the nucleus to induce oxidative phosphorylation, gluconeogenesis, fatty-acid oxidation, and antioxidant programs. This canonical node links sirtuins to energy expenditure, exercise response, and longevity, and is complemented by AMPK, which both activates PGC-1alpha directly and promotes SIRT1 activity through NAD+ elevation. Together these pathways coordinate mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility in response to nutrient and energy demand.
context.zh-TW: SIRT1 是一種 NAD+ 依賴性去乙醯酶，當被上升的 NAD+ 濃度激活時，會去乙醯化並激活轉錄輔激活因子 PGC-1alpha。PGC-1alpha 進而共同調節粒線體基因與清除活性氧的解毒酶，提升粒線體活性與生物生成，並帶來改善的代謝與抗氧化保護。此 SIRT1-PGC1alpha 軸將 NAD+ 前驅物攝取與粒線體健康連結起來，其作用標的包括 FOXO1 與 FOXO3a 轉錄因子。NR 與 NMN 透過此路徑改善粒線體功能、增強氧化代謝與能量消耗，並保護如 myocardium 等組織免於氧化壓力與細胞凋亡。

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: Through deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α, and cooperation with AMPK, SIRT1 promotes the transcription of nuclear- and mitochondrial-encoded respiratory-chain components, increasing mitochondrial number and function. This program expands oxidative capacity and supports the bioenergetic demands of muscle, liver, and brain. Directionally, SIRT1 and PGC-1α sit upstream of new mitochondrion formation. This program underlies many metabolic and neuroprotective benefits attributed to SIRT1 activation and to caloric restriction, and its decline with age contributes to the mitochondrial dysfunction associated with aging, metabolic disease, and neurodegeneration.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by mono-ADP-ribosylation, reducing conversion of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and limiting anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. Directionally, SIRT4 enzymatically suppresses GDH activity within mitochondria. This restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial ATP generation, marking SIRT4 as a metabolic brake in the organelle. Because SIRT4 also inhibits MTPα, glutamine metabolism, and PPARα signaling, it broadly opposes the oxidative, catabolic programs that SIRT3 promotes, and the antagonistic SIRT3/SIRT4 balance is emerging as an important determinant of mitochondrial health and metabolic resilience.

source_document: SIRT4.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 represses hypoxia-inducible factor 1alpha (HIF-1alpha) as a co-repressor (Zhong et al., 2010), suppressing downstream glycolytic and lipogenic programs and opposing the Warburg-like shift seen in cancer and aging. By limiting HIF-1alpha target transcription, SIRT6 favors oxidative metabolism and genomic stability, complementing its repression of c-MYC and its deacetylation of H3K9 and H3K56 at glycolytic promoters. Loss of SIRT6, seen in many cancer cell lines, derepresses glycolytic metabolism and supports tumor growth.

source_document: SIRT6.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 regulates rRNA transcription by activating RNA polymerase I and deacetylating histone H3K18 at ribosomal DNA, controlling ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of Pol I activity and ribosome production. Because excessive ribosome biogenesis fuels proliferation, this activity aligns SIRT7 with growth and, in cancer, with tumor promotion. It also ties SIRT7 to nucleolar stress responses and, through deacetylation of GABPβ1, to the transcriptional control of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes, such that SIRT7 deficiency causes systemic mitochondrial dysfunction with lactate accumulation and cardiac abnormalities.

source_document: SIRT7.md

subject: CD38

context.en-US: Inhibiting CD38, a major consumer of NAD+ that generates nicotinamide and cADPR, preserves cellular NAD+ pools by reducing their catabolic drain. Directionally, CD38 inhibition sits upstream of higher NAD+ availability. Because all sirtuins require NAD+ as an obligate co-substrate, preserving NAD+ indirectly sustains sirtuin activity across the family. This is a leading strategy to reverse age-related NAD+ decline, and CD38 expression rises with age, further depleting NAD+ and compromising sirtuin function. Pharmacologic CD38 inhibitors such as 78c restore NAD+ and sirtuin activity, and in aged male mice extend lifespan.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins (overview, CD38 KO risks, cancer therapies).md

subject: CD38

context.en-US: By preserving NAD+, CD38 inhibition boosts sirtuin activity, especially the mitochondrial sirtuin SIRT3, which depends on adequate NAD+ to deacetylate metabolic and antioxidant enzymes. Directionally, CD38 inhibition increases NAD+, which heightens SIRT3 function. This indirectly enhances mitochondrial ROS defense and metabolic health, and is consistent with observations that CD38 knockout mice show elevated NAD+ and increased SIRT1 activity with protection from diet-induced obesity. Pharmacologic CD38 blockers such as 78c extend lifespan in aged mice through this axis, making CD38 inhibition a key pharmacological lever on mitochondrial sirtuin biology.

source_document: SIRT3.md

subject: Daratumumab

context.en-US: Daratumumab (Darzalex, first approved 2015) and isatuximab (Sarclisa, approved 2020/2021) are IgG1 monoclonal antibodies that bind distinct epitopes on CD38, a cell-surface ectoenzyme. By engaging CD38 on malignant plasma cells, daratumumab triggers antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent killing. The directionality is the antibody acting on CD38-expressing cells. Although primarily an anticancer agent, depleting CD38 also reduces NAD+ consumption, indirectly favoring sirtuin activity.

source_document: Daratumumab.md

subject: Isatuximab

context.en-US: Isatuximab (Sarclisa) is an IgG1 anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, approved around 2020-2021, that binds a different CD38 epitope than daratumumab. It mediates direct apoptosis and immune effector functions such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis against CD38+ multiple myeloma cells. Directionally, the antibody engages CD38 to kill tumor cells. Like daratumumab, it also lowers CD38 ectoenzyme activity, indirectly preserving NAD+ for sirtuins. Isatuximab is used in combination regimens for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, and its anti-CD38 activity both depletes malignant plasma cells and reshapes the tumor microenvironment.

source_document: Isatuximab.md

subject: Daratumumab

context.en-US: Daratumumab is a frontline anti-CD38 antibody therapy for multiple myeloma, where CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells. Its clinical efficacy stems from direct and immune-mediated elimination of these cells, including complement-dependent cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis. Directionally, daratumumab sits upstream of myeloma cell clearance. Beyond oncology, its CD38 inhibition has the secondary effect of sparing NAD+ pools that sirtuins depend on, and it depletes CD38+ regulatory immune cells, reshaping the tumor microenvironment to restore anti-tumor T-cell and NK-cell responses.

source_document: Daratumumab.md

subject: Resveratrol

context.en-US: Resveratrol competitively inhibits cAMP phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4), the enzyme that degrades cAMP to AMP, thereby slowing cAMP clearance. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of PDE4 inhibition. This indirect action raises intracellular cAMP, which then engages the Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT cascade that further activates SIRT1 through NAD+ elevation. It is one arm of resveratrol's dual (direct plus indirect) SIRT1-activation mechanism, alongside allosteric binding to the SIRT1 N-terminal domain, and it explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even when direct binding is weak.

source_document: PDE4.md

subject: PDE4 inhibition (resveratrol)

context.en-US: Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, so intracellular cAMP accumulates after resveratrol exposure. Directionally, PDE4 inhibition leads to elevated cAMP. Elevated cAMP then activates the exchange protein Epac1, propagating a calcium and AMPK signal that ultimately boosts NAD+ and SIRT1. This pathway explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even through non-allosteric means, and it connects resveratrol's pharmacology to the broader cAMP signaling network. Because PDE4 is a validated therapeutic target, this arm also links resveratrol's metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects to a well-characterized drug target.

source_document: _document_ - berrougui2009_resveratrol_as_atheroprotective_compound.md

subject: cAMP (elevated)

context.en-US: High intracellular cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that triggers downstream signaling independent of PKA. Directionally, cAMP sits upstream of Epac1 activation. Epac1 then stimulates calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum, linking cAMP to Ca2+-dependent kinases and propagating a metabolic signal. This step is pivotal in resveratrol's indirect SIRT1-activation cascade, bridging the PDE4/cAMP arm to AMPK and NAD+ metabolism. The pathway illustrates how a polyphenol can activate sirtuins through classical second-messenger signaling rather than direct enzyme binding alone.

source_document: Epac1.md

subject: Epac1 activation

context.en-US: Epac1 activation induces calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, raising cytosolic Ca2+ that serves as a second messenger. Directionally, Epac1 sits upstream of cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation. The Ca2+ surge then activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), bridging cAMP signaling to AMPK activation. This couples resveratrol's PDE4 inhibition to metabolic kinase activation, and it is the key branching point that converts a rise in cyclic AMP into a change in cellular energy sensing. Disrupting any step in this cascade attenuates resveratrol's indirect activation of SIRT1.

source_document: Epac1.md

subject: Ca2+ surge (cytoplasmic)

context.en-US: The cytoplasmic calcium surge activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK, the central cellular energy sensor. Directionally, Ca2+ activates CaMKKβ, which in turn phosphorylates AMPK. Activated AMPK then induces NAMPT and raises NAD+, closing the loop on SIRT1 activation and promoting catabolic metabolism. This is a key branch point linking calcium flux to metabolic homeostasis, and it explains how agents that raise cytosolic calcium can indirectly boost sirtuin activity, complementing the direct actions of SIRT1 activators and integrating calcium signaling into energy metabolism.

source_document: AceCS1.md

subject: AMPK (activated)

context.en-US: Activated AMPK increases expression of NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway that converts nicotinamide to NMN. Directionally, AMPK sits upstream of NAMPT induction. More NAMPT elevates intracellular NAD+, the obligate co-substrate for sirtuins, and the AMPK-to-NAMPT-to-NAD+ axis is a major indirect route by which resveratrol, exercise, and caloric restriction activate SIRT1. Because NAMPT is rate-limiting, its induction is a decisive step in raising NAD+ availability, and AMPK and SIRT1 also induce each other, creating a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit that sustains NAD+-dependent processes.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: NAMPT upregulation

context.en-US: NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway, so its upregulation raises cellular NAD+ levels and fuels sirtuin activity. Directionally, NAMPT increase leads to NAD+ increase, which enhances sirtuin function. This is the terminal step of resveratrol's indirect activation cascade and a central control point for NAD+ homeostasis more broadly. Preserving NAD+ via NAMPT induction, or by inhibiting NAD+ consumers such as CD38 and PARPs, is a common theme across sirtuin-activating strategies, and it reflects the fact that cellular NAD+ availability, rather than sirtuin protein abundance alone, often limits sirtuin activity.

source_document: Dihydromyricetin.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO3a

context.en-US: Deacetylated FOXO3a transcriptionally upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes, prominently mitochondrial SOD2 and catalase, bolstering ROS scavenging. Directionally, SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a to drive increased antioxidant capacity. This reduces oxidative damage in resveratrol-treated cells and animals, and it is a central mechanism for sirtuin-mediated protection against aging and metabolic disease. The same FOXO3a-dependent antioxidant program is engaged by SIRT3 in mitochondria and is complemented by FOXO1- and FOXO4-mediated stress responses, establishing the sirtuin-FOXO axis as a primary node coupling nutrient sensing to cellular redox defense.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 deacetylates the NF-kB subunit RelA/p65 at Lys310 (Yeung 2004 PMID 15152190), preventing optimal DNA binding and transcriptional activation, and licenses p65 for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation, lowering both NF-kB activity and protein levels. This suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6. SIRT6 cooperates in constraining p65, and loss of SIRT1 or its decline with age allows NF-kB activity and chronic low-grade inflammation to rise, positioning the SIRT1-NF-kB axis as a key node in inflammaging and a mediator of resveratrol's anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular benefits.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 deacetylation of NF-κB

context.en-US: By deacetylating NF-κB, SIRT1 reduces transcription of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, dampening the inflammatory transcriptome. Directionally, SIRT1 deacetylation of NF-κB leads to lower cytokine output. This is mechanistically important in atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, and metabolic inflammation, where sustained cytokine signaling drives tissue damage. Resveratrol leverages this axis to curb chronic low-grade inflammation, and SIRT6, SIRT2, and SIRT7 also restrain NF-κB through distinct mechanisms, making suppression of NF-κB-dependent cytokine production one of the most consistent anti-inflammatory actions across the sirtuin family.

source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 (resveratrol-activated)

context.en-US: Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates and activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS activation in the endothelium. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone, protects against endothelial dysfunction, and reduces platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and French-paradox associations, and SIRT1's regulation of eNOS is one of its best-established vascular mechanisms, linking sirtuin activity directly to blood-vessel health and blood-pressure control.

source_document: SIRT1.md

subject: SIRT1 activation (resveratrol)

context.en-US: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. Directionally, SIRT1 activation sits upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation and is consistent with SIRT1s repression of lipogenic transcription factors such as SREBP-1c and PPAR-γ in the liver. By both increasing lipid catabolism and suppressing de novo lipogenesis, the pathway corrects the imbalance that drives non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

source_document: _document_ - berrougui2009_resveratrol_as_atheroprotective_compound.md

subject: Resveratrol
