context.zh-TW: BubR1 是一種紡錘體組裝檢查點蛋白，透過 SIRT2 在 Lys668 的去乙醯化而被穩定（SIRT2 下調加速 BubR1 降解）；SIRT2 過表達增加 BubR1 水平並延遲早衰小鼠的衰老表型，因此 BubR1 功能上是 SIRT2 通路的正向下游效應因子（North et al., 2014, Cell, PMID 24825348）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 deacetylates G6PD in the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) at Lys403, activating it to promote NADPH production and antioxidant defense; the PPP thus serves as a downstream effector of SIRT2 and is listed among its positive pathway regulators (Wang et al., 2014, Cell Metab, PMID 24769394).
context.zh-TW: SIRT2 在磷酸戊糖途徑（PPP）中去乙醯化 G6PD 的 Lys403，活化它以促進 NADPH 產生和抗氧化防禦；因此 PPP 作為 SIRT2 的下游效應因子被列為其正向通路調節因子（Wang et al., 2014, Cell Metab, PMID 24769394）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: As a class III NAD+-dependent deacetylase, SIRT2 activity is directly governed by NAD+ availability; NAD+ precursors (e.g., NMN, NR) boost SIRT2 activity in mitosis and metabolism, linking NAD+ decline in aging to reduced SIRT2 function (source review).
context.zh-TW: 作為第三類 NAD+ 依賴性去乙醯酶，SIRT2 的活性直接受 NAD+ 可用性控制；NAD+ 前體（例如 NMN、NR）在有絲分裂和代謝中增強 SIRT2 活性，將衰老中 NAD+ 的下降與 SIRT2 功能減弱聯繫起來（文獻綜述）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 deacetylates FOXO1 and FOXO3a, promoting their nuclear accumulation and target-gene activation (e.g., stress resistance, gluconeogenesis, and cell survival) in a manner analogous to SIRT1-FOXO coupling, making FOXOs downstream effectors and listed positive regulators of the SIRT2 pathway (Wang et al., 2007, PMID 17521387).
context.zh-TW: SIRT2 去乙醯化 FOXO1 和 FOXO3a，促進它們的核積累和靶基因活化（例如抗壓、糖質新生和細胞存活），類似於 SIRT1-FOXO 的耦合方式，使 FOXOs 成為 SIRT2 通路的下游效應因子和被列出的正向調節因子（Wang et al., 2007, PMID 17521387）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 promotes antioxidant defense in part through induction/stabilization of MnSOD (SOD2) targets, reducing mitochondrial superoxide; MnSOD is therefore listed among the positive regulators/effectors of the SIRT2 pathway in the source review's Table 3.
context.zh-TW: SIRT2 透過誘導/穩定 MnSOD（SOD2）靶點部分促進抗氧化防禦，減少粒線體超氧化物；因此 MnSOD 被列為文獻綜述表 3 中 SIRT2 通路的正向調節因子/效應因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: β-catenin (Wnt pathway) transcriptionally represses the SIRT2 promoter, and SIRT2 reciprocally deacetylates β-catenin to destabilize it, so Wnt signaling opposes SIRT2 pathway activity and vice versa in intestinal and cancer cell contexts (BBA Mol Cell Res 2021).
context.zh-TW: β-catenin（Wnt 通路）轉錄抑制 SIRT2 啟動子，而 SIRT2 相互去乙醯化 β-catenin 以不穩定化它，因此 Wnt 信號在腸道和癌細胞環境中拮抗 SIRT2 通路活性，反之亦然（BBA Mol Cell Res 2021）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: Akt signaling is associated with inhibition of SIRT2-dependent cell-cycle and stress outputs (e.g., cyclin E-CDK2 phosphorylates SIRT2 at Ser331 to reduce its deacetylase activity), placing AKT signaling among negative regulators of the SIRT2 pathway (Pandithage et al., 2008, J Cell Biol, PMID 18504304).
context.zh-TW: Akt 信號與 SIRT2 依賴性的細胞週期和壓力輸出的抑制相關（例如 cyclin E-CDK2 在 Ser331 處磷酸化 SIRT2 以降低其去乙醯酶活性），將 AKT 信號列為 SIRT2 通路的負向調節因子（Pandithage et al., 2008, J Cell Biol, PMID 18504304）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: NF-κB activation opposes SIRT2-dependent anti-inflammatory and cell-cycle programs, while SIRT2 deacetylates p65 to dampen NF-κB responses; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT2 pathway in aging.
context.zh-TW: NF-κB 活化拮抗 SIRT2 依賴性的抗發炎和細胞週期程序，而 SIRT2 去乙醯化 p65 以減弱 NF-κB 反應；表 3 將 NF-κB 列為衰老中 SIRT2 通路的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 is the principal mitochondrial deacetylase, regulating the majority of the mitochondrial acetylome to sustain oxidative-phosphorylation enzymes, fatty-acid oxidation, and the TCA/mitochondrial electron transport chain; SIRT3 declines with age, impairing mitochondrial function (source review; Hebert et al., 2013).
context.zh-TW: SIRT3 是主要的粒線體去乙醯酶，調節粒線體乙醯化組的大部分蛋白質以維持氧化磷酸化酶、脂肪酸氧化和 TCA/粒線體電子傳輸鏈；SIRT3 隨年齡下降，損害粒線體功能（文獻綜述；Hebert et al., 2013）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates SOD2 (MnSOD) at Lys68/Lys122 and supports glutathione-dependent antioxidant pathways, reducing mitochondrial ROS; aging-associated SIRT3 decline increases oxidative stress, and SIRT3 knockout mice show accelerated aging phenotypes (source review; Qiu et al., 2010).
context.zh-TW: SIRT3 在 Lys68/Lys122 處去乙醯化並活化 SOD2（MnSOD），支持穀胱甘肽依賴性的抗氧化通路，減少粒線體 ROS；衰老相關的 SIRT3 下降增加氧化壓力，SIRT3 敲除小鼠顯示加速的衰老表型（文獻綜述；Qiu et al., 2010）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 G477T and other SNPs are associated with human longevity/healthy aging; the G477T variant (V208I/V184I alleles) improves SIRT3 function or expression and is enriched in centenarian populations in some cohorts (source review; Rose et al., 2003, Alì et al., 2015 reports).
context.zh-TW: SIRT3 G477T 和其他 SNP 與人類長壽/健康衰老相關；G477T 變異（V208I/V184I 等位基因）改善 SIRT3 功能或表達，在某些族群中在百歲老人中富集（文獻綜述；Rose et al., 2003, Alì et al., 2015 報導）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: FOXO3a translocates to mitochondria where it binds the SIRT3 promoter and induces SIRT3 expression, which in turn activates MnSOD to reduce ROS, forming a FOXO3a-SIRT3-PGC-1α mitochondrial-protective loop (source review; Tseng et al., 2013; also PMC2532794).
context.zh-TW: FOXO3a 轉位至粒線體，在那裡結合 SIRT3 啟動子並誘導 SIRT3 表達，後者反過來活化 MnSOD 以減少 ROS，形成 FOXO3a-SIRT3-PGC-1α 粒線體保護迴圈（文獻綜述；Tseng et al., 2013；另見 PMC2532794）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: NF-κB (p65 at Ser536) occupies the SIRT3 promoter and represses SIRT3 transcription, so pro-inflammatory NF-κB activation lowers SIRT3 and mitochondrial antioxidant capacity; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway (Wang et al., 2021 preprint evidence).
context.zh-TW: NF-κB（p65 在 Ser536）佔據 SIRT3 啟動子並抑制 SIRT3 轉錄，因此促發炎的 NF-κB 活化降低 SIRT3 和粒線體抗氧化能力；表 3 將 NF-κB 列為 SIRT3 通路的負向調節因子（Wang et al., 2021 預印本證據）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: MAPK/ERK signaling can oppose SIRT3-dependent metabolic and antioxidant outputs (e.g., ERK-driven proliferative/fibrotic signaling coupling with SIRT3 decrease); Table 3 lists MAPK/ERK among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway in aging.
context.zh-TW: MAPK/ERK 信號可以拮抗 SIRT3 依賴性的代謝和抗氧化輸出（例如 ERK 驅動的增殖/纖維化信號與 SIRT3 下降耦合）；表 3 將 MAPK/ERK 列為衰老中 SIRT3 通路的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: PI3K/AKT signaling regulates Sirt3 in various contexts, generally opposing SIRT3-mediated catabolic/mitochondrial programs (e.g., PI3K/AKT modulates Sirt3 in activated microglia); Table 3 lists PI3K/AKT among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway (PMID 37930585).
context.zh-TW: PI3K/AKT 信號在多種環境中調節 Sirt3，通常拮抗 SIRT3 介導的分解代謝/粒線體程序（例如 PI3K/AKT 在活化的小膠質細胞中調節 Sirt3）；表 3 將 PI3K/AKT 列為 SIRT3 通路的負向調節因子（PMID 37930585）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 inhibits fatty-acid oxidation at the mitochondria by suppressing malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MCD) ADP-ribosylase activity and restraining oxidative fuel use, an adaptive suppression that rises under calorie restriction; during aging its dysregulation perturbs metabolic fuel selection (source review).
context.zh-TW: SIRT4 透過抑制丙二醯輔酶 A 脫羧酶（MCD）ADP-核糖基酶活性並抑制氧化燃料使用來抑制粒線體中的脂肪酸氧化，這種適應性抑制在熱量限制下升高；在衰老過程中，其失調干擾代謝燃料選擇（文獻綜述）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: SIRT4 suppresses apoptosis mainly by inhibiting mitochondrial glutamine metabolism (ADP-ribosylating GDH) and by dampening inducers such as PGC-1α/AMPK, protecting cells from genotoxic stress; SIRT4 loss in contexts like HCC promotes apoptosis, while its decline with stress affects tumor suppression and aging (source review).
context.zh-TW: SIRT4 主要透過抑制粒線體穀胺酸代謝（ADP-核糖基化 GDH）並減弱 PGC-1α/AMPK 等誘導因子來抑制凋亡，保護細胞免受基因毒性壓力；SIRT4 在 HCC 等環境中的缺失促進凋亡，而其隨壓力的下降影響腫瘤抑制和衰老（文獻綜述）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: NF-κB signaling suppresses SIRT4 in tumor and inflammatory contexts, consistent with the pro-inflammatory axis opposing SIRT4's tumor-suppressive and metabolic-restraining functions; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway.
context.zh-TW: NF-κB 信號在腫瘤和發炎環境中抑制 SIRT4，與促發炎軸拮抗 SIRT4 的腫瘤抑制和代謝限制功能一致；表 3 將 NF-κB 列為 SIRT4 通路的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: Pro-apoptotic Bax opposes SIRT4's anti-apoptotic effects on mitochondria; under stress Bax-mediated mitochondrial permeabilization is associated with decreased SIRT4-mediated protection, so Bax is listed among negative regulators of SIRT4 in Table 3.
context.zh-TW: 促凋亡 Bax 拮抗 SIRT4 對粒線體的抗凋亡作用；在壓力下，Bax 介導的粒線體通透化與 SIRT4 介導的保護減少相關，因此 Bax 被列為表 3 中 SIRT4 的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: Caspase activation, hallmark of the intrinsic apoptosis pathway, is antagonistic to SIRT4's mitochondrial anti-apoptotic function; during apoptosis caspases cleave/deregulate mitochondrial effectors, placing caspases among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway (Table 3).
context.zh-TW: Caspase 活化是內在凋亡通路的標誌，與 SIRT4 的粒線體抗凋亡功能相對抗；在凋亡期間，caspases 切割/失調粒線體效應因子，使 caspases 列為 SIRT4 通路的負向調節因子（表 3）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: GDH is the primary substrate through which SIRT4 suppresses glutamine metabolism, yet GDH is also listed among negative regulators in Table 3: high GDH activity can outpace SIRT4 ADP-ribosylation under energetic stress, switching cells toward glutaminolysis/fuel oxidation and away from SIRT4-mediated restraint.
context.zh-TW: GDH 是 SIRT4 抑制穀胺酸代謝的主要底物，但 GDH 也被列為表 3 中的負向調節因子：在能量壓力下，高 GDH 活性可能超過 SIRT4 的 ADP-核糖基化，使細胞轉向穀氨醯胺分解/燃料氧化，脫離 SIRT4 介導的限制。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4

context.en-US: AMPK activation (energy stress) opposes SIRT4's anabolic bias by promoting catabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis; reciprocal to SIRT4's inhibition of AMPK, AMPK signaling is thus classified among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway in Table 3.
context.zh-TW: AMPK 活化（能量壓力）透過促進分解代謝和粒線體生成來拮抗 SIRT4 的合成代謝偏向；與 SIRT4 抑制 AMPK 相互對應，AMPK 信號因此被歸類為表 3 中 SIRT4 通路的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 regulates fuel oxidation via desuccinylation/deglycylidation of mitochondrial enzymes including CPS1 and components of fatty-acid oxidation, supporting metabolic flexibility under fasting and during aging; its age-related changes affect liver and muscle energetics (source review; Park et al., 2013).
context.zh-TW: SIRT5 透過去琥珀酰化/去甘氨醯化粒線體酶（包括 CPS1 和脂肪酸氧化的組成成分）來調節燃料氧化，支持禁食和衰老過程中的代謝靈活性；其與年齡相關的變化影響肝臟和肌肉能量學（文獻綜述；Park et al., 2013）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 desuccinylates enzymes of the urea cycle and electron-transport chain to sustain mitochondrial function under ammonia and oxidative stress, mitigating accumulation of damaged mitochondria with age; it also supports antioxidant capacity during fasting (source review; Nakagawa et al., 2009).
context.zh-TW: SIRT5 去琥珀酰化尿素循環和電子傳輸鏈的酶以在氨和氧化壓力下維持粒線體功能，減輕受損粒線體隨年齡的積累；它還在禁食期間支持抗氧化能力（文獻綜述；Nakagawa et al., 2009）。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 inhibits apoptosis, thereby opposing SIRT5's pro-survival species; in Table 3 Bcl-2 is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT5 pathway in contexts where SIRT5's effects depend on cell survival/Apoptosis signaling.
context.zh-TW: 抗凋亡 Bcl-2 抑制凋亡，因此拮抗 SIRT5 的促存活作用；在表 3 中，Bcl-2 被列為 SIRT5 通路在 SIRT5 效果依賴於細胞存活/凋亡信號環境中的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 desuccinylates GDH to inhibit its activity (opposite to SIRT4, which ADP-ribosylates GDH), so high GDH activity counters SIRT5-dependent restraint of glutamine metabolism; GDH is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT5 pathway in Table 3.
context.zh-TW: SIRT5 去琥珀酰化 GDH 以抑制其活性（與 SIRT4 ADP-核糖基化 GDH 的作用相反），因此高 GDH 活性對抗 SIRT5 依賴性的穀胺酸代謝限制；GDH 被列為表 3 中 SIRT5 通路的負向調節因子。

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 desuccinylates pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) to suppress its activity, favoring glutamine-dependent anaplerosis over glucose oxidation; PDH activity is thus reciprocally regulated and listed among negative regulators/opponents of SIRT5's metabolic program in Table 3 (Park et al., 2013, PMC3769971).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 overexpression extends lifespan in male mice and is required for healthy aging, acting through DNA repair, metabolic regulation, and inflammation control; as with SIRT1, SIRT6 activity is NAD+-dependent and declines with age (Kanfi et al., 2012, Nature; source review).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 functions in DNA repair; as the nuclear/chromatin sirtuin it guards genome integrity, telomeres, metabolism, and inflammation (Mostoslavsky 2006; Mao 2011 PMID 21680843). It is a core DNA double-strand-break repair factor: recruited to DSBs, it deacetylates H3K9/H3K56 and CtIP and stimulates PARP1 to promote homologous recombination and genomic stability (Kaidi et al., 2010, PMC2943420).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 on telomeric chromatin and suppresses LINE-1 retrotransposon activity, maintaining genome stability and telomere function; SIRT6-deficient cells show genomic instability, telomere defects, and cellular senescence (Michishita et al., 2008; Van Meter et al., 2014).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at telomeres and stabilizes WRN helicase, preventing telomere dysfunction-induced senescence; SIRT6-depleted cells undergo accelerated telomere replication problems and senescence (Michishita et al., 2008, Cell; source review).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: Nrf2, the master antioxidant transcription factor, induces SIRT6-responsive antioxidant and DNA-repair programs; SIRT6 binds the Nrf2 promoter and cooperates with Nrf2 to maintain glutathione and redox balance, and Nrf2 deacetylation is itself regulated by SIRT6 (Pan et al., 2016, Cell Res).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: In the vasculature, eNOS/NO signaling and SIRT6 cooperate in endothelial protection and vasodilation (analogous to the SIRT1-eNOS loop), so eNOS is listed as a positive regulator of the SIRT6 pathway in Table 3.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: IGF-1/AKT signaling can modulate SIRT6 activity and expression in metabolic and intestinal-fitness contexts, generally promoting SIRT6-dependent metabolic and tumor-suppressive programs; Table 3 lists IGF-1/AKT among positive regulators of the SIRT6 pathway.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: p21 (CDKN1A), whose expression is antagonized by SIRT6 (SIRT6 suppresses p21-driven senescence), accumulates with age and opposes SIRT6-regulated cell-cycle and DNA-repair programs; Table 3 lists p21 among negative regulators of SIRT6 (source review).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 on NF-κB (p65) target-gene promoters to repress NF-κB-dependent inflammation, and conversely NF-κB activation opposes SIRT6's anti-inflammatory/genome-stability program in aging; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of SIRT6 (Kawahara et al., 2009, Cell).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: ICAM-1, an endothelial/leukocyte adhesion molecule elevated during inflammation and aging, is a target of SIRT6-repressed NF-κB signaling; its upregulation opposes SIRT6's vascular-protective role and it is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT6 pathway in Table 3.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: PAI-1 is transcriptionally repressed by SIRT6 through H3K9 deacetylation at its promoter (SIRT6 binding is a hallmark of PAI-1 downregulation), so PAI-1 elevation with age opposes SIRT6's anti-senescence and metabolic programs; Table 3 lists PAI-1 among negative regulators of SIRT6 (Van Meter et al., 2014).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 deacetylates H3K18 on promoters (Barber et al., 2012, Nature, PMID 22722849) and associates with chromatin remodelers (including PAF1 complex) to regulate rDNA transcription, ribosomal biogenesis, and global gene expression; age-related SIRT7 decline perturbs these epigenetic landscapes (source review; Vakhrusheva et al., 2008).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 promotes cellular stress resistance by suppressing ER stress and reactive-ROS programs via Myc-linked silencing of ribosomal protein genes and by stabilizing DNA repair; SIRT7-depleted cells show increased apoptosis and metabolic stress (Shin et al., 2013, PMID 24210820; source review).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 is required for RNA polymerase I transcription and cell survival: its knockdown reduces Pol I association with rDNA and triggers apoptosis, and it deacetylates p53 in HCC cells to dampen p53-driven apoptosis, linking SIRT7 decline to age-related apoptosis and disease (Ford et al., 2006, Genes Dev 20:1075; source review).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: FOXO3 is a positive regulator of the SIRT7 pathway: FOXO factors interact with SIRT7 to promote stress resistance, while SIRT7 deacetylates FOXO3 to prevent pro-apoptotic Ser574 phosphorylation, forming a mutual-activation loop (source review Table 3; SIRT7-FOXO3 cooperation).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: The SIRT7-Myc axis is bidirectional: SIRT7 assembles with Myc at ribosomal protein (RP) gene promoters to silence gene expression and relieve ER stress, while Myc-driven proliferation opposes SIRT7-dependent growth-quiescence programs in some contexts; Table 3 lists Myc among negative regulators of SIRT7 (Shin et al., 2013, PMID 24210820).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 suppresses HIF-1α/2α protein levels (deacetylation-coupled destabilization), reducing hypoxic gene activation, and reciprocally HIF-1α is listed as a negative regulator of the SIRT7 pathway, an opposition relevant to tumor metabolism and aging (Hubbi et al., 2013, PMC3774348).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 deacetylates p53 to repress p53-driven apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma, and p53 activation reciprocally opposes SIRT7 functions (e.g., under genotoxic stress p53 promotes apoptosis despite SIRT7), so p53 is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT7 pathway (source review; oncogene review s41388-024-02976-8).

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 catalyzes removal of acetyl groups from β-catenin, and this deacetylation suppresses β-catenin's ability to activate transcription and drive cell proliferation. The modification dampens the Wnt transcriptional output of the protein at target promoters. This is one of the tumor-suppressive arms of SIRT1 in cancer, complementing its deacetylation of the RelA/p65 NF-κB subunit. Directionality is enzymatic: SIRT1 is the deacetylase and β-catenin the substrate, and the net effect is reduced oncogenic transcriptional signaling.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2 disruption

context.en-US: Disruption of SIRT2 in the mouse raises the levels of the mitotic regulators Aurora-A and Aurora-B, leading to aneuploidy and mitotic cell death. Because SIRT2 is a tubulin deacetylase and a guardian of mitotic fidelity, its loss impairs the control that normally keeps Aurora kinase abundance in check during division. The directionality is that SIRT2 sits upstream: reduced SIRT2 permits Aurora kinase accumulation, which then destabilizes mitosis. This pathway connects sirtuin biology to chromosome segregation and genomic instability in tumorigenesis.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2-deficient mice

context.en-US: SIRT2-deficient mice develop gender-specific tumors, with females acquiring mammary tumors and males developing hepatocellular carcinoma, matching the mitotic instability produced by elevated Aurora-A/Aurora-B. Consistent with a tumor-suppressor role, human breast cancers and hepatocellular carcinomas often show reduced SIRT2 relative to normal tissue. The relationship is directional: loss of SIRT2 predisposes to these malignancies, whereas SIRT2 expression restrains them. This positions SIRT2 among the sirtuins that act as tumor suppressors in genetic mouse models.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT3 deficiency

context.en-US: In mice and cultured cells, SIRT3 deficiency favors cell transformation in response to oncogenic Ras or Myc, and the same loss stabilizes HIF-1α with consequent induction of the glycolytic program of the Warburg effect. Because SIRT3 normally governs mitochondrial metabolism, ROS production, and genome stability, its absence releases a permissive environment for oncogenic signaling and metabolic reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT3 acts upstream: reduced SIRT3 allows transformation and Warburg metabolism to proceed, defining its tumor-suppressive role in this context.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT6 overexpression

context.en-US: Acute overexpression of SIRT6 in cancer cell lines of different histology induces apoptosis, supporting a tumor-suppressive role for this nuclear sirtuin. The pro-apoptotic activity appears linked to SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase function rather than its deacetylase activity. Directionally, increasing SIRT6 abundance or enzymatic activity triggers cell death in tumor cells. This contrasts with SIRT1's context-dependent duality and stresses that sirtuin outputs in cancer depend on the specific isoform and its dominant catalytic modality.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 inhibits cellular senescence and apoptosis in c-Myc- and PML-driven cancers by deacetylating and inactivating p53 and proapoptotic FOXO transcription factors and by sequestering Bax via deacetylated Ku70. These actions blunt the tumor-suppressive programs that would otherwise eliminate premalignant cells. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity is upstream of senescence suppression, protecting cells from growth arrest. Consequently, SIRT1 inhibitors are frequently anticancer on their own and sensitize cancer cells to anticancer agents or oxidative stress.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2 downregulation
object: p53 accumulation and cell cycle arrest

context.en-US: SIRT2 downregulation or chemical inhibition induces anticancer effects that include p53 accumulation, cell cycle arrest, and apoptosis, mirroring the tumor-suppressive functions of the enzyme. Loss of SIRT2 permits mitotic regulators such as Aurora-A/Aurora-B to accumulate, destabilizing division and forcing checkpoint engagement. The relationship is directional: reduced SIRT2 activity leads to p53 stabilization and arrest. A caveat is that SIRT2 inhibition can be counterproductive in some contexts, notably alongside microtubule inhibitors where it prolongs chronic mitotic arrest and confers resistance.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: AC93253

context.en-US: AC93253 is a small molecule that inhibits SIRT2 at micromolar concentrations. In leukemia cells, SIRT2 inhibition with AC93253 is accompanied by Akt acetylation, de-phosphorylation, and consequent inhibition, producing antileukemia effects. The directionality is that AC93253 blocks SIRT2, which then removes deacetylation-based control over Akt, shifting it toward an inactive state. This positions AC93253 as both a research tool for SIRT2 biology and an anticancer lead, and connects sirtuin inhibition to PI3K/Akt pathway suppression.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2 inhibition

context.en-US: SIRT2 inhibition or downregulation appears counterproductive in certain cancer contexts, particularly when combined with microtubule inhibitors, because loss of SIRT2 prolongs chronic mitotic arrest and makes cancer cells resistant to these agents. The enzyme normally helps cells exit mitosis cleanly; without it, cells linger in a prolonged arrested state that selects for survival. Directionally, low SIRT2 activity sits upstream of this resistance phenotype. This caveat limits the general anticancer rationale for SIRT2 inhibition and argues for careful context- and regimen-specific use.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: In oral squamous cell carcinomas, SIRT3 is overexpressed, and its downregulation has antiproliferative activity and sensitizes carcinoma cells to radiation and to cisplatin. This contrasts with SIRT3's broader tumor-suppressive role in mouse models, showing that sirtuin function is context-dependent. Directionally, elevated SIRT3 supports tumor growth and therapy resistance in this cancer type, while SIRT3 loss restores sensitivity. The finding highlights that a single sirtuin can be either protective or oncogenic depending on tumor type and molecular background.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 promotes tumorigenesis by deacetylating lysine 18 of histone H3, thereby repressing genes with tumor-suppressor function. SIRT7 is stabilized at target promoters through interaction with the ETS-family transcription factor ELK4, and the resulting H3K18 deacetylation is necessary to maintain features such as anchorage-independent growth and loss of contact inhibition. Directionally, SIRT7 activity at H3K18 sits upstream of tumor suppressor gene repression. Loss of SIRT7 reduces the tumorigenicity of human cancer xenografts, making it the clearest pro-oncogenic sirtuin and positioning SIRT7 inhibition as the therapeutic direction.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: ELK4

context.en-US: The ETS-family transcription factor ELK4 interacts with SIRT7 and stabilizes the deacetylase at target gene promoters, allowing SIRT7 to deacetylate histone H3 at lysine 18 and repress tumor-suppressor genes. This tethering is required to maintain cancer hallmarks such as anchorage-independent growth and loss of contact inhibition. Directionally, ELK4-bound promoter occupancy precedes SIRT7-dependent H3K18 deacetylation. SIRT7 depletion accordingly reduces the tumorigenicity of human cancer xenografts, highlighting the ELK4-SIRT7-H3K18 axis as an oncogenic regulatory circuit.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Sirtuins

context.en-US: The conserved catalytic core of sirtuins features a large Rossmann fold domain typical of NAD+ binding proteins, together with a small zinc-binding domain and flexible loops that bring the two domains together around an extended cleft for cofactor and substrate. The Rossmann domain contains six parallel beta-strands and a Gly-X-Gly phosphate-binding motif. Directionally, this architecture is intrinsic to the sirtuin family and explains their strict NAD+ dependence. Understanding the structure underscores why NAD+ analogs and pocket C binders act as sirtuin modulators.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Sirtuin NAD+ binding site

context.en-US: The sirtuin NAD+ binding site is divisible into an adenine binding pocket (pocket A), a nicotinamide ribose pocket (pocket B), and a nicotinamide binding pocket (pocket C), formed by the large Rossmann domain and the cofactor binding loop. NAD+ enters a non-productive conformation outside the C pocket until an acetyl-lysine substrate is present, at which point a productive arrangement engages the C pocket. Directionally, this topology defines how inhibitors such as nicotinamide (pocket C) and suramin (pockets B, C, and substrate site) act, and frames structure-based design of sirtuin modulators.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: The crystal structure of human SIRT6 reveals a more open conformation than other sirtuins, with the small domain displaced and the cofactor binding loop replaced by a stable single helix. Kinetic and structural data indicate SIRT6 is the unique sirtuin able to bind NAD+ in the absence of an acetyl-lysine substrate. This raises the possibility that SIRT6 evolved away from a conventional NAD+-dependent deacetylase toward a NAD+ metabolite sensor function. Directionally, this distinctive structural feature sets SIRT6 apart from SIRT2, SIRT3, and SIRT5 and informs the search for SIRT6-specific modulators.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Nicotinamide

context.en-US: Nicotinamide, a product of the sirtuin deacetylation reaction itself, is a micromolar non-competitive inhibitor of SIRT1 and SIRT2 that interacts with the C (nicotinamide) pocket of the catalytic site. It was one of the first endogenous compounds studied as a sirtuin inhibitor and inspired the search for NAD+ and nicotinamide analogs. SIRT1 inhibition with nicotinamide was reported to have anticancer activity in B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia and prostate cancer. Its limitations, and those of NAD+ analogs, lie in modest potency and limited therapeutic potential, which motivated development of more potent scaffolds.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Sirtinol
object: Breast, lung, prostate and leukemia cancer cells

context.en-US: Sirtinol, a hydroxynaphthaldehyde derivative discovered in a phenotypic screen, is active against multiple sirtuin isoforms and has cytotoxic activity against cancer cells of different origins, including breast, lung, prostate, and leukemia cell lines. This broad anticancer activity made sirtinol the founding member of the beta-naphthol inhibitor family and seeded structure-activity programs that produced salermide, cambinol, and splitomicin. Directionally, sirtinol-mediated inhibition of sirtuin activity sits upstream of its cytotoxic effects on malignant cells, though its full target spectrum extends beyond sirtuins.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: EX-527

context.en-US: EX-527, the most potent and selective SIRT1 inhibitor identified from a large high-throughput screen, inhibits SIRT1 at nanomolar concentrations with remarkable selectivity over SIRT2 and SIRT3 and good pharmacokinetic properties. Its anticancer activity as a single agent is weak, but it cooperates with HDAC inhibitors to induce apoptosis in leukemia cells. Directionally, EX-527-mediated SIRT1 blockade combined with broad HDAC inhibition produces a synergistic lethal effect. This positions EX-527 as the standard pharmacological SIRT1 inhibitor and a component of combination anticancer strategies.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Ro31-8220

context.en-US: Ro31-8220, a bisindolylmaleimide originally developed as a protein kinase C inhibitor, was identified by screening known kinase inhibitors against SIRT2 on the rationale that sirtuins and protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site. It showed SIRT1/SIRT2 inhibitory properties in the low micromolar range. Directionally, the shared adenosine scaffold allows this kinase inhibitor to engage sirtuin NAD+ binding. Because it retains potent kinase activity, Ro31-8220 serves as both a probe of sirtuin biology and a caution about off-target effects in sirtuin inhibitor studies.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: GW5074

context.en-US: GW5074, an indolinone compound originally developed as a c-Raf kinase inhibitor, was tested with other kinase inhibitors against SIRT2 because sirtuins and protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site. It showed SIRT1/SIRT2 inhibitory properties in the low micromolar range, placing it alongside the bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 as a kinase-scaffold sirtuin inhibitor. Directionally, GW5074's scaffold enables engagement of the sirtuin NAD+ pocket. Its continued kinase activity complicates interpretation in cells, underscoring the value of structure-based follow-up for selectivity.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: NF675

context.en-US: NF675 is the product of optimizing the suramin scaffold and is the most potent and selective molecule in the series, showing a 20-fold selectivity ratio for SIRT1 over SIRT2. Suramin itself inhibits SIRT1/SIRT2 at nanomolar concentrations with apparent SIRT1 preference, has anticancer activity, and has been studied in clinical trials. Directionally, NF675 inherits suramin's binding mode while improving isoform selectivity. Despite good potency and selectivity, suramin-derived compounds have modest drug-likeness owing to high molecular weight and anionic character, limiting therapeutic translation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Suramin
object: SIRT5 pockets B, C and substrate-binding site

context.en-US: Co-crystallization of suramin with human SIRT5 revealed that suramin binds by occupying the nicotinamide ribose pocket (B-pocket), the nicotinamide pocket (C-pocket), and part of the substrate-binding site. This structural insight explains suramin's broad, high-affinity inhibition of multiple sirtuins and informed the design of more selective derivatives such as NF675. Directionally, suramin is the ligand and the SIRT5 catalytic cleft the receptor. The structure also illustrates general principles governing small-molecule engagement of the sirtuin NAD+/substrate channel.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Aristoforin

context.en-US: Aristoforin is one of several natural products reported to inhibit sirtuins at micromolar concentrations, alongside amurensin G, polyphenols, and tanikolide. These compounds expand the chemical diversity of sirtuin inhibitors beyond synthetic scaffolds. Directionally, aristoforin blocks sirtuin deacetylase activity at micromolar potency. As with many natural-product sirtuin modulators, target selectivity, mechanism, and additional cellular targets are less characterized than for synthetic inhibitors, so the anticancer contributions of sirtuin inhibition versus other effects remain to be disentangled.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Amurensin G

context.en-US: Amurensin G is a resveratrol tetramer natural product reported among compounds that inhibit sirtuins at micromolar concentrations and endowed with anticancer activity. It belongs to a series that includes aristoforin, polyphenols, and tanikolide identified through general screens of structurally diverse natural products. Directionally, amurensin G suppresses sirtuin deacetylase activity. Its isoform selectivity and mechanism are incompletely characterized, and its anticancer effect may involve both sirtuin inhibition and additional natural-product bioactivities.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Tanikolide

context.en-US: Tanikolide is a natural product reported to inhibit sirtuins at micromolar concentrations, grouped with aristoforin, amurensin G, and polyphenols as structurally diverse natural sirtuin inhibitors. Directionally, tanikolide blocks sirtuin deacetylase activity at micromolar potency. As with companion natural products, its selectivity and the biological significance of its sirtuin inhibition relative to other targets remain less well studied than for synthetic inhibitors such as EX-527 and the tenovins.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6

context.en-US: Tenovins (tenovin-1 and tenovin-6) are sirtuin inhibitors that block SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation of p53, leading to p53 hyperacetylation and activation. Their strong anticancer activity is associated with this p53 activation, which reinstates tumor-suppressive transcription in cancer cells. Directionally, tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition sits upstream of p53 activation and tumor suppression, a property shared with HDAC inhibitors and other p53-releasing strategies. Tenovins illustrate the direct link between sirtuin inhibition, p53 acetylation state, and cancer therapy.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Butein

context.en-US: Butein is a polyphenolic chalcone that was among the first small molecules reported to activate SIRT1, together with resveratrol, piceatannol, quercetin, and myricetin. These polyphenolic STACs (compounds 1-5 of the review's activator figure) established the concept of pharmacological SIRT1 activation. Directionally, butein and its polyphenol congeners enhance SIRT1 deacetylase activity, at least in biochemical assays. As with resveratrol, the in vivo activation mechanism is debated, since activation of SIRT1 by these compounds could frequently only be demonstrated with fluorescently tagged substrates, suggesting possible assay artifacts or indirect cellular effects.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SRT1460

context.en-US: SRT1460 is a potent, chemically diverse second-generation sirtuin-activating compound reported alongside SRT1720 and SRT2183 as more effective activators than the polyphenolic STACs. Most compounds of this class were also reported to have anticancer activity. A major caveat is that the mechanism of SRT1460 action remains unclear: activation could frequently only be demonstrated with fluorescently tagged substrates, and the metabolic effects may reflect indirect actions (e.g., via the cAMP-Epac1-AMPK axis) rather than direct SIRT1 binding. Directionally, SRT1460 enhances SIRT1 activity in assay systems, but interpretation of in vivo effects requires caution.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SRT2183

context.en-US: SRT2183 is a potent second-generation sirtuin-activating compound identified with SRT1720 and SRT1460 as chemically diverse, more potent activators than the initial polyphenolic STACs. These compounds were reported to have anticancer activity, but their mechanism is controversial: activation was frequently demonstrable only with fluorescently tagged substrates, and metabolic effects may be indirect (cAMP-Epac1-AMPK pathway) rather than direct SIRT1 activation. Directionally, SRT2183 stimulates SIRT1 deacetylase activity in biochemical assays. These caveats frame the ongoing debate about the physiological relevance of STAC-mediated SIRT1 activation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: STACs

context.en-US: A matter of controversy is that sirtuin activation by resveratrol and the SRT compounds could frequently only be demonstrated with fluorescently tagged substrates, raising the possibility of assay artifacts. Alternative explanations invoke indirect activation: resveratrol activates SIRT1 in vivo through its effect on cAMP signaling, specifically the cAMP-Epac1-AMPK pathway, and other STACs may act similarly given their analogous metabolic effects. Directionally, the claimed direct SIRT1 activation by STACs is questioned, and their in vivo benefits may be mediated by other pathways. This controversy shaped the rigorous characterization of STAC chemistry and calls for non-fluorescent assay confirmation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Sirtuin Fluorimetric Activity

context.en-US: Sirtuin fluorimetric activity assays (e.g., the Fluor de Lys system) are the most commonly used methods to screen molecules as sirtuin inhibitors. Deacetylation of a fluorophore-decoupled substrate sensitizes it to a developer that releases a measurable fluorophore, and percent inhibition is calculated from fluorescence. These assays identified indoles (EX-527), tenovins, JGB1741, sirtinol analogues, and cambinol analogues. A key caveat is that the aminomethylcoumarin moiety of the fluorogenic substrates can affect binding of other small molecules to the enzyme, so confirmation with orthogonal assays is recommended.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Suramin-related compounds

context.en-US: The homogeneous fluorescent deacetylase assay, which uses the fluorescent acetyl-lysine substrate ZMAL and NAD+ followed by trypsin treatment to release the AMC fluorophore, was used to screen several compound families as sirtuin inhibitors, including adenosine mimetics, inhibitors of kinases or phosphatases, suramin analogs, splitomicin derivatives, thiobarbiturates, and 3-arylideneindolin-2-ones. Directionally, the assay's ZMAL-ZML trypsin-coupled readout provides a plate-compatible screen for sirtuin inhibition. Its utility explains the breadth of scaffolds identified across independent discovery programs.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Charcoal Binding Assay

context.en-US: The charcoal binding assay measures sirtuin activity by quantifying 3H-labeled OAADPr released as free acetate: incubation of recombinant sirtuins with a 3H-acetylated peptide and NAD+ produces 3H-OAADPr, which binds activated charcoal, but the 3H-acetate hydrolyzed from OAADPr remains in the supernatant and is counted. This method was used to screen nicotinamide analogs and NAD+ metabolites as inhibitors of SIRT2. Directionally, the assay traces sirtuin catalytic flux through its unique OAADPr by-product rather than through fluorophore release, giving an artifact-free alternative to fluorescent assays.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Microfluidic mobility shift assay

context.en-US: The microfluidic mobility shift assay separates SIRT1 substrate and product peptides by differences in electrophoretic mobility caused by charge and mass changes upon lysine deacetylation, quantitating fluorescence of both peaks. The assay effectively separates neutral-acetylated substrate peptides from deacetylated products bearing an additional positive charge. Although it could support high-throughput screening, it is more suitable for hit confirmation and mechanistic studies. Directionally, it provides a label-based yet artifact-minimized readout of SIRT1 activity distinct from fluorophore-release assays.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: NAD+ bioluminescence assay

context.en-US: The NAD+ bioluminescence assay measures sirtuin activity by quantifying remaining NAD+ after a deacetylation reaction, coupling NAD+ consumption to bacterial luciferase-catalyzed oxidation of decanal via a NAD+/NADH reduction step. It uses a label-free peptide substrate and is applicable to sirtuins with any peptide substrate. Directionally, NAD+ depletion tracks sirtuin catalytic turnover. Its label-free nature and high amenability to high-throughput screening make it a useful complement to fluorescent substrate-based assays, whose artifacts affect STAC measurements.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Radiochemical nicotinamide release assay

context.en-US: The radiochemical assay measures sirtuin deacetylase activity using an acetylated peptide substrate and [carbonyl-14C]-NAD+, detecting the release of 14C-nicotinamide. Unreacted NAD+ is captured by a boronic acid resin, and the unbound fraction containing released nicotinamide is counted in a scintillation counter, in a format compatible with 96-well high-throughput screening. Directionally, radiolabeled nicotinamide release directly quantifies catalytic rounds. This assay confirmed the identification of indoles as sirtuin inhibitors, although radioactive waste and safety considerations limit routine screening use.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Enzyme-coupled nicotinamide assay

context.en-US: The enzyme-coupled assay for nicotinamide detection measures sirtuin activity continuously by coupling nicotinamidase (which hydrolyzes nicotinamide to nicotinic acid and ammonia) to glutamate dehydrogenase, which converts ammonia, alpha-ketoglutarate, and NAD(P)H to glutamate and NAD(P)+, quantified spectrophotometrically at 340 nm. It was developed in 2009 and, while not used yet on the scale of large screenings, could be adapted to a high-throughput format. Directionally, a continuous enzyme-coupled readout avoids the artifacts associated with fluorescent and end-point assays.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Western blot analysis

context.en-US: Western blot is the most commonly used cell-based analysis to evaluate sirtuin inhibition: cells are exposed to putative inhibitors, lysed, and probed with antibodies against acetylated lysine on known sirtuin substrates, typically p53, histone 3, or gamma-tubulin. Increased acetylation indicates reduced sirtuin activity. Directionally, the acetylation state of these substrates reports the functional outcome of inhibitor treatment in intact cells. Because it measures endogenous substrates rather than artificial fluorophores, it is a key confirmatory readout after fluorescent screening.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Cell-based ELISA assay

context.en-US: The cell-based ELISA-type assay, adapted from histone acetyltransferase inhibitor assays, confirms SIRT2 inhibitors such as 3-arylideneindolin-2-ones: cells seeded in 96-well plates are treated with compounds, fixed, permeabilized, and probed with antibody against acetylated alpha-tubulin, with fluorescence measured after enhancement solution addition. This format is well suited for high-throughput screenings. Directionally, the acetylated tubulin signal directly reflects SIRT2 deacetylase inhibition in cells. It complements Western blot with quantitative, plate-based throughput.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Capillary electrophoresis-based sirtuin assay

context.en-US: Recently, non-peptide substrates for SIRT1 have been synthesized, and two capillary electrophoresis assays were developed and validated to monitor the deacetylation of these substrates and to screen sirtuin inhibitor activity, complementing earlier CE assays using N-terminally fluorescence-labeled peptides. Directionally, CE separates substrate and product by their charge/mass differences without relying on fluorophore-release effects. The non-peptide substrates broaden the assay chemistry available for studying SIRT1 and its modulators.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: JGB1741

context.en-US: JGB1741 is a small-molecule SIRT1 inhibitor developed on the sirtinol structure and identified with other sirtinol analogues through sirtuin fluorimetric activity assays. As a sirtinol derivative, it is expected to block SIRT1 deacetylase activity, promoting hyperacetylation of substrates such as p53. Directionally, JGB1741 engages the SIRT1 catalytic site to inhibit deacetylation. Its derivation from the sirtinol scaffold places it within the beta-naphthol family of sirtuin inhibitors, whose anticancer activities derive substantially from p53 reactivation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin that functions as a tubulin deacetylase, removing acetyl groups from alpha-tubulin to regulate microtubule dynamics and mitotic fidelity. Because it deacetylates tubulin and other mitotic regulators, SIRT2 loss impairs the control that normally keeps Aurora-A and Aurora-B in check during division, leading to aneuploidy and mitotic cell death. Directionally, SIRT2's tubulin deacetylase activity is an upstream determinant of normal chromosome segregation, linking sirtuin biology to mitotic stability and tumor suppression.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: ELK4

context.en-US: ELK4 (SAP-1) belongs to the ETS-domain ternary complex factor (TCF) subfamily of transcription factors, defined by a conserved ETS DNA-binding domain. Within sirtuin biology, ELK4 is notable for interacting with SIRT7 and stabilizing the deacetylase at target gene promoters, where SIRT7 deacetylates lysine 18 of histone H3 and represses tumor suppressor genes. Directionally, ELK4's identity as an ETS factor underlies its promoter-targeting function. This links the ETS transcription factor family to the pro-oncogenic SIRT7-H3K18ac axis in cancer.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: ELK1

context.en-US: ELK1 is the founding member of the ternary complex factor subfamily of ETS-domain transcription factors, alongside ELK3 and ELK4 (SAP-1), and is a major nuclear target of the RAS-MAPK/ERK cascade that controls immediate-early gene expression. In the context of sirtuin biology it serves as the canonical reference for the ETS-TCF family whose member ELK4 stabilizes SIRT7 at target promoters. Directionally, ELK1's ETS DNA-binding domain and SRF-coupling architecture are shared by the TCF family, informing how ELK4 anchors SIRT7 to chromatin for H3K18 deacetylation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: ETS

context.en-US: ETS is a large family of eukaryotic transcription factors sharing a conserved winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding ETS domain that recognizes purine-rich GGAA/T core motifs and regulates proliferation, differentiation, and oncogenesis. The ETS-family member ELK4 plays a central role in sirtuin biology by stabilizing SIRT7 at target gene promoters, enabling H3K18 deacetylation and repression of tumor suppressor genes. Directionally, the ETS family provides the DNA-binding and promoter-targeting mechanisms that members such as ELK4 use to recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes such as SIRT7.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Sirtuins

context.en-US: Sirtuins and protein kinases both contain an adenosine-binding pocket in their catalytic machinery, an overlap that allowed screening of known kinase inhibitors against SIRT2. This shared scaffold led to the discovery that bisindolylmaleimides such as Ro31-8220 and indolinones such as GW5074 inhibit SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range. Directionally, the shared adenosine site is the molecular basis for cross-inhibition between kinase inhibitors and sirtuins, but it also means these compounds retain kinase activity, complicating the attribution of cellular effects to sirtuin inhibition alone.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 is stabilized at the promoters of its target genes through interaction with the ETS-family transcription factor ELK4, which tethers the deacetylase to chromatin. Once anchored, SIRT7 deacetylates lysine 18 of histone H3 (H3K18ac), repressing tumor suppressor genes and maintaining cancer hallmarks such as anchorage-independent growth and loss of contact inhibition. Directionally, ELK4-mediated stabilization precedes and enables SIRT7's H3K18 deacetylation. Consistent with this axis, SIRT7 depletion reduces the tumorigenicity of human cancer xenografts, underscoring the ELK4-SIRT7 connection as a therapeutic vulnerability.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Butein

context.en-US: Butein is a chalcone polyphenol that belongs to the first generation of natural sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs), reported to activate SIRT1 together with resveratrol, piceatannol, quercetin, and myricetin. These polyphenolic activators established the concept of pharmacological SIRT1 activation and served as the basis for later, more potent synthetic STACs such as SRT1460, SRT1720, and SRT2183. Directionally, butein's identification as a polyphenol STAC initiated the activator chemistry that progressed to synthetic scaffolds, though the direct activation mechanism remains controversial due to fluorescent-substrate artifacts.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SRT1460

context.en-US: SRT1460 is a second-generation synthetic sirtuin-activating compound (STAC) of the imidazothiazole class, developed with SRT1720 and SRT2183 as chemically diverse and more potent activators than the initial polyphenolic STACs. These compounds were reported to have anticancer activity, but their mechanism is controversial: activation could frequently only be demonstrated with fluorescently tagged substrates, and in vivo effects may be indirect (e.g., via the cAMP-Epac1-AMPK pathway) rather than direct SIRT1 binding. Directionally, SRT1460 belongs to the synthetic STAC class whose biology underlies the ongoing debate about STAC-mediated SIRT1 activation.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SRT2183

context.en-US: SRT2183 is a second-generation synthetic sirtuin-activating compound (STAC) identified alongside SRT1720 and SRT1460 as a chemically diverse, potent SIRT1 activator that followed the polyphenolic STACs resveratrol, piceatannol, butein, quercetin, and myricetin. These compounds were reported to have anticancer activity, but their activation mechanism is debated because activity was frequently only demonstrable with fluorescently tagged substrates, and metabolic benefits may reflect indirect actions (cAMP-Epac1-AMPK) rather than direct SIRT1 binding. Directionally, SRT2183 belongs to the synthetic STAC class whose mechanism remains an open question.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Ro31-8220

context.en-US: Ro31-8220 is a bisindolylmaleimide compound originally developed as a protein kinase C inhibitor; its adenosine-binding scaffold allowed it to be repurposed as an inhibitor of SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range. It belongs to the kinase-inhibitor scaffolds identified by screening known kinase inhibitors against sirtuins, sharing this property with the indolinone GW5074. Directionally, Ro31-8220's identity as a kinase-inhibitor scaffold underlies its cross-reactivity with sirtuins through the shared adenosine-binding site. Because it retains potent kinase activity, cellular effects cannot be attributed solely to sirtuin inhibition.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: GW5074

context.en-US: GW5074 is an indolinone compound originally developed as a c-Raf kinase inhibitor; like the bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220, it was repurposed as a sirtuin inhibitor after screening known kinase inhibitors against SIRT2 based on the shared adenosine-binding site between sirtuins and kinases. GW5074 shows SIRT1/SIRT2 inhibitory activity in the low micromolar range. Directionally, its identity as a kinase-inhibitor scaffold enables engagement of the sirtuin NAD+ pocket. Its continued kinase activity complicates interpretation in cells, highlighting the need for selectivity optimization in dual kinase/sirtuin inhibitor design.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: NF675

context.en-US: NF675 is a suramin-derived small molecule that is the most potent and selective compound in its scaffold series, showing a 20-fold selectivity ratio for SIRT1 over SIRT2. It was obtained through optimization of the suramin scaffold, which itself is a nanomolar inhibitor of SIRT1/SIRT2. Directionally, NF675's identity as a suramin-derived, SIRT1-selective inhibitor illustrates scaffold engineering for isoform selectivity within the sirtuin inhibitor field. Its modest drug-likeness, stemming from high molecular weight and anionic character, limits therapeutic application despite good potency and selectivity.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 is inhibited by kinase-inhibitor scaffolds identified by screening known kinase inhibitors against the enzyme on the rationale that sirtuins and protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site. The bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 and the indolinone GW5074 showed SIRT1/SIRT2 inhibitory properties in the low micromolar range, alongside the general Kinase enzyme family that shares the adenosine pocket. Directionally, the shared adenosine-binding site of SIRT2 and protein kinases underlies this cross-inhibition. Because these scaffolds retain kinase activity, their cellular effects reflect a combination of kinase and sirtuin blockade.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Kinase

context.en-US: Protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site with sirtuins such as SIRT2, an overlap exploited by screening known kinase inhibitors against sirtuins as a drug-discovery strategy. This shared adenosine pocket allows scaffolds like the bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 and the indolinone GW5074 to engage both families, inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range while retaining kinase activity. Directionally, the enzyme superfamily of Kinase proteins and sirtuin deacetylases both rely on an adenosine-binding pocket, explaining the cross-reactivity between kinase-inhibitor scaffolds and sirtuins. This structural convergence frames interpretation of kinase-inhibitor effects in sirtuin biology.

source_document: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md

subject: Curcumin

context.en-US: The review highlights natural compounds, especially curcumin, as candidates to activate or otherwise regulate sirtuins, positioning them as low-toxicity anti-ageing interventions. Directionally, curcumin is upstream as a putative sirtuin modulator. A caveat is that the review frames this as a hope/area of active research rather than established clinical efficacy, and sirtuin activation by curcumin remains less mechanistically defined than for resveratrol.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: miR-34a

context.en-US: The 3'UTR of the SIRT1 transcript contains a miR-34a-responsive element; active miR-34a represses SIRT1 translation. Directionally, miR-34a sits upstream to lower SIRT1 protein. Because SIRT1 deacetylates and inhibits p53, this repression is part of a negative feedback loop that helps explain the drop in SIRT1 observed during senescence.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: p53

context.en-US: Active p53 transcriptionally induces miR-34a, a tumor-suppressive microRNA. Directionally, p53 is upstream of miR-34a expression. miR-34a then feeds back to repress SIRT1 translation, coupling the p53 damage-response program to the sirtuin-NAD+ axis.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: NF-κB

context.en-US: NF-kB can decrease SIRT1 activity by modulating miR-34a expression, mirroring the p53-miR-34a-SIRT1 loop. Directionally, NF-kB engagement of the miR-34a arm suppresses SIRT1 translation. This provides a route by which chronic inflammatory signaling blunts sirtuin activity during ageing.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction raises the level of almost all sirtuins except SIRT4; SIRT2 is among those increased by CR (observed in white fat and kidney of CR mice). Directionally, CR is the upstream stimulus and elevated SIRT2 a downstream mediator. This generalizes the CR-sirtuin axis beyond SIRT1/SIRT3.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction raises SIRT3 levels, consistent with SIRT3's role as a mitochondrial metabolic sensor engaged during CR and fasting. Directionally, CR increases SIRT3 abundance/activity. This supports the view that CR benefits are mediated across the sirtuin family, not only SIRT1.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction increases SIRT5 levels alongside other sirtuins (except SIRT4). Directionally, CR is upstream of elevated SIRT5. SIRT5 desuccinylates/demalonylates metabolic enzymes, so its CR induction fits the broader CR-driven remodeling of mitochondrial acylation.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction increases SIRT6 levels; SIRT6 is otherwise depleted in senescent fibroblasts and vascular cells. Directionally, CR raises SIRT6, supporting its genome-stability and metabolic functions. This aligns SIRT6 with the CR- and healthspan-protective sirtuin program.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Caloric Restriction

context.en-US: Caloric restriction increases SIRT7 levels; SIRT7 otherwise declines in senescent fibroblasts. Directionally, CR is upstream of elevated SIRT7. Given SIRT7's nucleolar/ribosomal and stress roles, its CR induction extends sirtuin-mediated adaptation to the nucleolus.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT2

context.en-US: SIRT2 levels rise in senescent cells regardless of trigger (stress, oncogene, replicative exhaustion) but not in quiescent or apoptotic cells, and SIRT2 is not required to induce senescence. Directionally, senescence causes elevated SIRT2 rather than vice versa. This makes SIRT2 a useful biomarker of the senescent state.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: SIRT1 binds the P66shc promoter and deacetylates histone H3 there, reducing P66shc transcription and lowering this pro-oxidant adaptor. Directionally, SIRT1 suppresses P66shc. This axis lowers mitochondrial ROS and is a plausible contributor to the ~30% lifespan extension seen in P66shc knockout mice, and to calorie-restriction benefits.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: P66shc

context.en-US: P66shc inhibits the activity of the FOXO3a transcription factor, blunting a key stress-resistance and antioxidant program. Directionally, P66shc suppresses FOXO3a output. Because SIRT1 represses P66shc, sirtuin activity indirectly unleashes FOXO3a-dependent defense pathways.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: P66shc

context.en-US: P66shc knockout mice live about 30% longer than wild-type controls and show enhanced resistance to oxidative stress and age-related pathologies, indicating P66shc is a negative regulator of longevity. Directionally, loss of P66shc extends lifespan. This makes P66shc an attractive node, with SIRT1 as an upstream suppressor, for longevity interventions.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT6

context.en-US: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at telomeric regions in response to DNA damage and stabilizes the WRN helicase at telomeres, tightening telomere structure and preventing dysfunction during replication. Directionally, SIRT6 maintains telomere integrity. Loss of SIRT6 causes H3K9 hyperacetylation and chromatin relaxation at telomeres, tying it to genomic stability in ageing.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: Under stress the nuclear fraction of SIRT3 deacetylates H4K16 and H3K9, regulating expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolism. Directionally, SIRT3 acts enzymatically on chromatin in the nucleus. This reveals a nuclear, chromatin-level face of the otherwise mitochondrial sirtuin, complementing its metabolic roles.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT5

context.en-US: SIRT5 desuccinylates superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), increasing its activity and thereby enhancing cytosolic antioxidant defense. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates SOD1. This extends sirtuin control of antioxidant enzymes beyond SIRT3's activation of mitochondrial MnSOD/IDH2.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT7

context.en-US: SIRT7 deacetylates histone H3 at K18 (and H2A/H2B), an activity associated with repression of tumor-suppressor genes; SIRT7 thereby helps sustain the cancer phenotype without driving transformation. Directionally, SIRT7 enzymatically remodels chromatin to favor oncogenic transcription. This links nucleolar SIRT7 to tumor biology.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: In mouse oocytes aged in vivo or in vitro, expression of SIRT1, SIRT2 and SIRT3 is dramatically reduced; prolonged expression of these sirtuins reduces postovulatory oocyte ageing. Directionally, loss of SIRT3 (with SIRT1/2) accompanies oocyte ageing. SIRT1 and SIRT3 act as redox sensors in oocytes, implicating them in female fertility and age-related reproductive decline.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: Aged mouse oocytes show sharply reduced SIRT1 (together with SIRT2 and SIRT3); maintaining SIRT1 expression reduces postovulatory oocyte ageing in vitro and in vivo. Directionally, SIRT1 decline contributes to oocyte ageing. This positions SIRT1 among the sirtuins guarding oocyte redox state and female fertility.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT1

context.en-US: In humans, lower serum SIRT1 levels are associated with frailty compared with non-frail individuals, suggesting circulating sirtuins as a non-invasive frailty marker. Directionally, the association is correlative: reduced SIRT1 tracks frail phenotype. A caveat is that this is a biomarker correlation, not proof of causality.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: Alongside SIRT1, lower serum SIRT3 levels are associated with frailty in older individuals, supporting serum sirtuins as a candidate non-invasive frailty biomarker. Directionally, the association is correlative. Longitudinal validation is needed, but the finding motivates sirtuin-level monitoring in ageing cohorts.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: Nicotinamide

context.en-US: Nicotinamide (NAM), a product of the sirtuin deacetylation reaction, is a non-competitive feedback inhibitor of sirtuin activity. Directionally, NAM accumulation suppresses the very enzymes that produce it, gating sirtuin flux by the NAD+/NAM ratio. This feedback is a key reason NAD+ availability (and NAMPT salvage vs PARP1 consumption) limits sirtuin activity in ageing.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: NAMPT

context.en-US: NAMPT, the rate-limiting NAD+ salvage enzyme, is regulated by the CLOCK:BMAL1 circadian complex, coupling NAD+ biosynthesis and thus sirtuin activity to the daily rhythm. Directionally, the CLOCK/BMAL1 loop drives rhythmic NAMPT and NAD+ levels. This explains the circadian gating of sirtuin-dependent processes and links clock disruption to altered sirtuin activity.

source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: Among the seven mammalian sirtuins, SIRT3 is the only isoform directly linked to human longevity, supported by a VNTR-enhancer polymorphism in the SIRT3 gene associated with survival at oldest ages. Its predominant mitochondrial localization and central role in energy metabolism make it a critical regulator of mitochondrial function and metabolic adaptation. This longevity association distinguishes SIRT3 from SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT6, which influence healthspan through other mechanisms, and motivates the review's focus on SIRT3 as a geroscience-relevant target.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2) at Lys413 (Yu 2012 PMID 22416140), boosting NADPH biosynthesis. Under caloric restriction and dietary restriction, SIRT3-mediated IDH2 deacetylation elevates NADPH, regenerating glutathione and lowering mitochondrial ROS; loss of SIRT3 abolishes this DR-dependent antioxidant response and exacerbates metabolic disease. The resulting NADPH fuels antioxidant regeneration and prevents electron transport chain overload, curbing ROS and potentiating mitochondrial antioxidant capacity. This SIRT3-IDH2-NADPH axis couples nutrient sensing to mitochondrial redox homeostasis and preserves cochlear hair cells under caloric restriction.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 regulates succinate dehydrogenase (SDH, complex II), described as a critical acetylation node within the mitochondrial matrix that mediates crosstalk between metabolic flux control and mitochondrial energy transduction systems. Through modulation of SDH enzymatic activity, SIRT3 fine-tunes substrate utilization efficiency while maintaining electron transfer chain synchronization, preserving metabolic homeostasis across the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation interface.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: Beyond canonical deacetylase activity, SIRT3 possesses substantial lysine decrotonylase capacity, selectively removing crotonyl groups from specific histone substrates. This dynamic regulation of histone crotonylation adds a new dimension to SIRT3's epigenetic repertoire, modulating gene expression plasticity under both homeostatic and stress conditions. The review positions this decrotonylase activity alongside SIRT3's roles in heterochromatin maintenance and double-strand break repair as a nuclear epigenetic function of the mitochondrial deacetylase.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 decreases H3K27 crotonylation at metastasis-associated loci such as the ETS1 promoter, effectively constraining neoplastic dissemination. Mechanistically, the long noncoding RNA LINC00922 can decoy SIRT3 away from the ETS1 promoter, upregulating local H3K27 crotonylation and driving colorectal cancer metastasis. This places SIRT3's lysine decrotonylase activity at the interface of histone acylation state and oncogenic transcription.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 facilitates DNA double-strand break repair by enhancing the recruitment of 53BP1, thereby promoting the efficiency of non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). It also promotes H3K56 deacetylation to enhance NHEJ fidelity, and interacts with critical DNA repair proteins such as PARP1, Ku70/80, XRCC1, and DNA ligase 4 to repair mitochondrial and genomic DNA damage. This nuclear DNA-repair program complements SIRT3's mitochondrial antioxidant function in maintaining genomic stability and preventing cellular senescence (Fig. 1B).

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 maintains heterochromatin integrity in human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), postponing replicative senescence. It forms macromolecular assemblies with nuclear lamina constituents and heterochromatin-associated proteins supporting chromatin compaction and genomic stability. Absence of SIRT3 triggers structural abnormalities in the nuclear envelope, disarray of heterochromatin organization, and reactivation of silenced repetitive sequences, accelerating premature cellular aging; restoration of SIRT3 re-establishes chromatin organization and mitigates senescence phenotypes.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: SIRT3 mediates its anti-fibrotic effect through targeted deacetylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3beta) at Lys15, effectively preventing Smad3 transcriptional complex formation and subsequent fibrogenic programming. Genetic deletion of SIRT3 increases GSK3beta acetylation and hyperactivates TGF-beta signaling, culminating in enhanced transcription of ECM-related genes. This mechanism operates across peritoneal, cardiac, pulmonary, and hepatic fibrosis models.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3

context.en-US: In cardiomyocytes, SIRT3 attenuates fibrosis by inhibiting the FOS/AP-1 and STAT3/NFATc2 signaling pathways, complementing its GSK3beta Lys15 deacetylation that blocks Smad3 complexes. Together these transcriptional suppressions reduce ECM gene expression and pathological cardiac remodeling, establishing SIRT3 as a master anti-fibrotic node acting on multiple pro-fibrotic pathways simultaneously.

source_document: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
